Hello,
**My name is Eileen Laubacher, and I am the Democrat and retired U.S. Navy Rear Admiral running against Lauren Boebert here in Colorado.**
I was 17-years-old the first time I raised my right hand and took an oath to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic.
I took those words, and that responsibility, seriously every day for the next 4 decades. When I was an intelligence officer. When I was deployed to Afghanistan. When I became an Admiral. And as a member of the president’s National Security Council.
But in all those years, I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, and our very democracy as I do right now. I said I would never run for office. But in this moment, I feel an obligation to step up, serve my community, and defend our country once again.
**I am running for Congress to defeat Lauren Boebert because when she was sworn into office, Lauren took a similar oath to defend our Constitution – and she has betrayed it almost every single day since then.**
Adam Frisch only lost to Lauren Boebert by 546 votes. It was the closest race in the entire country. With the right Democrat, we can finally put an end to Lauren Boebert’s embarrassing political career – but I need your help now to do it.

subject: The NYPD called it terrorism. CNN called them teenagers.
body:
Plus: Trump says there's "practically nothing left to target" in Iran | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
Two ISIS-inspired men threw IEDs packed with explosives at Americans in New York City. The NYPD called it terrorism. [CNN called them "Pennsylvania teenagers"](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=31c356541e&e=567664f14c) enjoying "abnormally warm weather."

---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=412e290b46&e=567664f14c)
| |
🔥 **CNN CALLED ISIS TERRORISTS "PENNSYLVANIA TEENAGERS" — THEN DELETED IT**
The NYPD Commissioner held a press conference. Crystal clear: ISIS-inspired. Admitted it on camera. Admitted it in custody. No ambiguity whatsoever.
Then CNN tweeted about two teenagers from Pennsylvania who crossed into New York City "for what could have been a normal day." The backlash was immediate. They deleted the tweet. Then Abby Phillip went on air and said the bombs were aimed at the mayor — also wrong. She had to correct herself the next morning and blamed her producers.
**Mark lays out the full timeline. Layer after layer. This isn't incompetence — it's a pattern.**
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=0861747555&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
📊 **69% OF DEMOCRATS SAY AMERICA IS NOT A FORCE FOR GOOD**
A new poll breaks it down by party: 91% of Republicans say America is a force for good. 69% of Democrats say it's not. Independents split 50-50.
When nearly three-quarters of one party thinks their own country is bad — and you look at who's feeding them information — the connection is impossible to ignore.

🏛️ **HAALAND CRUSHES BREGMAN 73-27 — EXCLUSIVE POLLING COMING SUNDAY**
Haaland won the Democratic pre-primary convention with 73.5% of the delegate vote. Mark says the closest this primary will be is 15-20 points.
But here's the tease: Mark has been told exclusive polling data on the Democratic race is coming — at least one poll, possibly two. The big question: has the Epstein flight moved the needle at all? Tune in Sunday.

⚠️ **IRAN — "PRACTICALLY NOTHING LEFT TO TARGET"**
Trump told Axios the war is "way ahead of timetable" and there is "practically nothing left." Netanyahu is calling on Iranians to rise up. The new Ayatollah hasn't been seen.
Iran's one play left is disrupting oil markets — they're hitting tankers and mining the Strait. The US has destroyed 16 mine-laying vessels. Gas is up 60-80 cents. Mark thinks within a week, Trump or Netanyahu tells the Iranian people it's time.

Peter, I want to tell you something I don’t talk about much.
When you’re deployed to a combat zone, you get phone calls home. Not many. And they’re short. The connection is bad, the timing is worse, and you spend half the call pretending everything is fine so the people you love don’t worry.
**_My mom knew I wasn’t telling her the true situation._**
She knew that “I’m fine, mom” meant rockets had targeted the base that week. She knew that “it’s quiet here” meant I couldn’t tell her what was actually happening. And she knew that every time I said “I’ll be home soon,” there was a chance I wouldn’t be.
That’s the part of military service that doesn’t make the campaign ads.
We talk about the soldier. We don’t talk about the mom who can’t sleep. The dad who checks his phone every 30 minutes. The family who has to wonder if their loved ones will be home for Christmas this year.
My family lived that. For nine months while I was in Iraq, they carried the weight of not knowing if I’d make it home.
And they’re not special. They’re one of thousands of military families across this country who sacrifice in silence while politicians in Washington use the troops as props in photo ops and then forget they exist the second the cameras turn off.
I’m running for Congress because military families deserve more than a yellow ribbon magnet on someone’s bumper.
They deserve a representative who actually understands what it’s like. Who’s been on both sides of that phone call. Who knows that “supporting the troops” doesn’t mean clapping at an airport — it means fixing the VA, fighting for military spouse employment, making sure no veteran sleeps on a park bench, and making sure the men and women we send into harm’s way have a government that’s worthy of their sacrifice.
_**That’s what this campaign is about.**_
_**Not me. Not my Bronze Star. Not my resume.**_
_**The families.**_
Every mom who can’t sleep. Every kid who doesn’t understand why their parent is gone. Every veteran who comes home to a system that doesn’t care.
I’m fighting for them. And I’m asking you to fight with me. **Please, chip in whatever you can.**

That’s what this campaign is about. Not me. Not my Bronze Star. Not my resume. The families. Every mom who can’t sleep. Every kid who doesn’t understand why their parent is gone. Every veteran who comes home to a system that doesn’t care. I’m fighting for them. And I’m asking you to fight with me. Please, chip in whatever you can. _Media contact:_[_Info@VoteRonEller.com_](mailto:Info@VoteRonEller.com)

**_Ron Eller Declares Victory in MS-02 Republican Primary_**

**_Unofficial Results are “Mathematically Improbable” for Opponent to Win_**

_Raymond, MS_ – Today, the Ron Eller Campaign officially announced victory in the Republican Primary for Mississippi’s Second Congressional District. With the final numbers clearly in focus, it is now mathematically impossible for remaining uncounted absentee ballots to change the outcome of Tuesday's election, decisively settling the primary in Eller's favor.

The election returns show Eller won a commanding 22 out of the 30 counties in the district. This widespread geographic support—from Warren and Hinds to Bolivar and Yazoo counties—cements a clear mandate from Republican voters across MS-02 and demonstrates a broad, united coalition heading into the general election.

**"I am deeply humbled and honored by the trust the voters of the Second District have placed in me again to be their Republican nominee,"** Eller said. **"Kevin Wilson ran an honorable race and is a good public servant for the people of Adams County. Our district is better for his participation in this process."**

With the primary now settled, the Eller campaign is calling for total unity among Mississippi Republicans in the Second District.

**"Now is the time to come together as one party with one shared mission,"** Eller continued. **"The primary is now behind us, and our sights are now set squarely on November. For far too long, Congressman Bennie Thompson has left the people of Mississippi’s Second District behind. Though former President Biden was forced to pardon Bennie Thompson for his wrongdoing this congressional term, I’m hopeful that the people of the second district will not pardon him again. It is time for a new generation of leadership aligned with President Trump that will fight for economic growth, secure borders, voter integrity and the constitutional rights of every Mississippian. We welcome every Kevin Wilson supporter to our team—together, we are going to unseat Bennie Thompson this fall."**

For more information on Ron Eller’s platform and upcoming campaign events, please visit [https://www.voteroneller.com/](https://voteroneller.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cadf08ca3f7559848c17d00e3&id=42a9147928&e=a56613e05b)

subject: The reality of running a campaign

body:
#

Peter —
Let me guess: when you open up your email inbox, you're bombarded with emails from political campaigns or advocacy organizations, some of which you've never heard of.
I know it's a lot. And it's why in a sea of promises that "Donald Trump is FINISHED" and breathless "5X MATCH NOW!!!" emails, I work really hard to make sure our messages are different.
So today, I wanted to take a moment to pull back the curtain and explain why we send emails asking you for money and where your donation goes.
In 2021, my campaign raised a record-breaking $162 million _(all thanks to your support!)_ but Republicans spent over $269 million to try to defeat me. I ended up winning my runoff election by just over 1%, an extremely small margin.
I share these numbers with you because the reality is, we have to be prepared for Republicans to spend _even more_ this time around to try to replace me with some henchman who will do Trump's bidding, no questions asked.
Trump and Republicans started this year with more than $600 million cash on hand. They're sitting on a huge war chest that they're ready to spend to maintain their grip on power for years to come. **And I'm their #1 target for defeat.**
Peter, my campaign won't accept contributions from corporate PACs or federal lobbyists. That means the vast majority of the donations that fuel this campaign come from emails just like this one. People chipping in $10, $25, or $50 at a time.
And the money we raise _right now_ means we mobilize more voters in every corner of the state, place more ads to spread my message across Georgia, and hire more staff to sustain and even expand our efforts.
And while I certainly don't expect you or anyone else to donate to every email my team and I send, I hope you'll consider donating to this one.
So here's the part where I ask: [**Can you please make a contribution to my reelection campaign today? When you have people like Trump in power — who act outside of the law — the only solution is absolute victory in the midterm elections.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-mar26.B6mAX1&refcode=em260313-1-subs&t=1&akid=1832%2E5691347%2E-li3Dq)

subject: The latest on Trump’s immigration policy
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROB BONTA FOR CALIFORNIA ATTORNEY GENERAL 2026 FPPC ID #145642
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Immigrants are part of the fabric of this country. They are part of our families, our communities, and our history.
But since the moment Donald Trump returned to the White House, his administration has been enacting a cruel anti-immigrant agenda, complete with their own mass deportation machine.
The President has broken the law and violated the Constitution in service of his anti-immigrant agenda over and over again. And when he breaks the law, we fight back.
Right now, we’re working against Trump’s illegal no-bond immigration detention policy, and I want to share an update on where things stand:
→ This week, I filed an amicus brief to challenge the Trump administration’s unlawful new interpretation of decades-old immigration law.
Our immigration system has long included access to bond hearings. But under Trump’s policy, this right is eliminated — mandating indefinite detention for some non-citizens without the opportunity for a bond hearing, and regardless of any individual circumstances.
We’re talking about many undocumented immigrants who care for dependent young children, who have family members who are U.S. citizens, who have been here for decades and have deep roots in the community, and who have no criminal history.
As enforcement has surged, denying more and more people consideration for bond has led to dangerously overcrowded detention facilities with unsafe conditions that no just system should accept.
Indefinite detention without due process is inhumane — and it violates the Constitution and decades of immigration law.
None of us can stand by while the federal government strips away human rights and undermines due process. As Attorney General, I’ll keep fighting to protect our values and our neighbors.
But I can’t do it alone. I’m relying on my strongest grassroots supporters like you to support my campaign when we need it most. Right now, we’re working towards our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline. Will you contribute before the end of March to power my re-election campaign and this important work? It is now no longer a question of whether Colorado will attempt to redistrict but of whether or not our measure will succeed.
What will determine the success of the redistricting in Colorado is twofold:
First, it is a matter of whether or not Coloradans have the resolve to endure an all out assault from the administration aimed at pressuring them to back off and could include:

* Cuts to federal funding and disaster relief during the Summer fire season

* Increased ICE presence, raids and attacks on Coloradans citizens and non-citizens alike, and even National Guard Deployments.

* Election interference and more

Trump used this playbook against California last summer in an attempt to stop Governor Newsom's Prop. 40 redistricting effort and it failed. The President's attempts to coerce us will fail too. No matter the costs, Coloradans will not bow.
However, to get this effort on the ballot, we will need to gather signatures from 2% of registered voters in all of Colorado's 35 State Senate Districts, nearly 200,000 people.
Getting these 200k+ signatures will take thousands of signature gatherers and a massive GOTV apparatus. A lowball estimate for how much this will cost comes in at $3,000,000. And right now we are behind on raising this.
Coloradans are ready to grit our teeth and pay the enormous cost retribution but we can't let it be for nothing. Will Democrats from across the country fall in behind us and help to shoulder the enormous cost of getting this on the ballot?
We are confident that the answer to this is yes.

## TSA Workers See Paychecks Stop
TSA agents will miss their first full paycheck today as the Department of Homeland Security shutdown drags into its [fourth week with no](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwRsWXPwRDwxdvKVrR-sGLjYthsjcxMrbV-krdD7ST0f_r-tyxZhiXj9xJ8uhLJnOmoiZjiWXO75CObjiUdghM7ofzJ4XUDBIZaQ2i8eYXkvXeBuIgExDVo-jMdMwmEuzWT1A36lxAqfpNlLoHRlDAftbN7lO9020b00ZbbTSyvStuih9gQGMGqeOwiA6RT5yOdrvEjNvFNKrPOloXdmbZDfmexXmQ8AsYD7Ps3X55t6jgPlNC5iVETBrEDBXysgk_VblVnZKmL2s24N9ObMMj-xjXiVXlHHf43ogx5LbjffUHNbfz5hSrMMoOrXuGNPfBf5Xt6eF3wAAAP__1gWBSg) deal in sight. Major airports, including Denver and Seattle-Tacoma, are now [collecting donations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd1jAcfxTUKSxtEW2XW1lnYVDzAaDBdxYfvsr5xVuN9JIn-abP4_lgT74-PyNG-nq0hLpKIFqpbzEtOPpUq4Fc6oGa0XzwmjrooTquQAuYbHow7l0jdWOSBE0pOUwAEx9D2OzagL4140TiBEdWANAwo6EvZyMlANi4_VFEyBBCing1opRyFH1CsQwdeR61gmyvqbc_k8-1pVcONObcmvS1gS91roXBnemZqbm4zjarcSrY2qmyL8KU_MlxdT8yejzfjnxjCGc3KXMbYpYfYqFY-GOLGUM_Ej5Rblwh4b45kshy3c8zUrm9eFkfr_Lv_Vx-9VkbffDh-BLP7BOPDf04TOv_ujTt1bfAQAA___V-YyO) of gift cards and have begun stocking food pantries for TSA workers. Unscheduled absences among security officers have more than doubled, [over 300 employees have quit,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OrSAYxJ8GOwx_PCoFxW3szm23NAgfR3YRXPg8xrffuK-w3SSTmcz8Pp7z04QY0uu_2UCjz3OCs0ZAhDKnvJvL54LVlIzWIBr7ZZLDWTDRUyYpl7MzIV5z1zjtAQTIBjQfBilV38uxWbV4LEZ5ZdUIchDWKjVwWMYOgNnF-a4J-m5jkkvOOJOPlo2Mj6IXkg2qA9-TjoELmEv7mUPCFXy88htKa_PWRL0i7pXIf0RMREznebZ2qfeL2ydiuiURE1ZDzVIhWajU5WOJQOt6oMtnopIx-n0EpCaUPRekFexRAl40hgR3vCna7WeIMdR-IB17bSbE3wX4J2xvLX4CAAD__2NNg20) and some airports have seen hours-long lines at security checkpoints during the spring break travel surge. Senate Democrats on Thursday [defeated a motion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE-DOyJ42NguKLZxl223tDA8YjYYInhJ5NuvvFf46xnN6Pv-3Ne7jSnmx297oKFQ1ozflpAI65rLy56hVGq2FnKWyLqnzZ5WEKC5UFyq1duYzrXvvAmIgKpDI8dRqVlrNXW7AYlawxb6SYxhQjnPo5rnYRi20MPmfBfNtSaUVFJIoYabmIScQIMS49xj0KwX6COVevtbYqYdQzrLB-vNlaNLZid6NaZ-MVgYLLTjHlO6MgbLXg68gBgsDbMlZLAM4yTlMHCPR3HVUuNbKu7Z-FVONnve0L1rpJOHd_YxP_gWU2KwdNX41zemFJseWS8eh43_nzr6kbqPgX8BAAD__8p9gt4) to proceed to a House-passed bill to reopen DHS and end the shutdown. The two sides remained deadlocked over conditions for immigration enforcement.
## Iran's New Leader Issues First Statement
Iran's new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, issued his [first public statement Thursday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiPbzRgIHFwy2V56IWpwe_GusZHdM4i_P3G6P9iopCqpVPX-fMwfGGJIn79xJ8s-z4nOGomZypzygZfPhSuWzCsy4_qNyfGspTZCglAwOwzxmvvWWU-kCVqyahgAJmNgbDeLyki5aC_J0ei0nxQ-wDzGBSaSXvo22LtNggIllYRHJ0epRm00yGHqyZuml-QC59J95ZB4Ix-v_KbSrXlvo92Yj9rAr0Y_G_08z7NLy3q_uPPbySW6Rj9DwfRfqkh0ivo6Cu0kIqGjIvb8xbig-N5wp0RB-EDlEj6UyuJ4LTGsojIy7ZRYlDWhNqCgb4t1xxliDNUMTS8_dwzx3zb-EdC31X8DAAD__7rKjFM), vowing to avenge every Iranian killed in the war and declaring the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed. He didn't appear on camera, and reports have circulated that the 56-year-old is [in a coma with](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O3DAMhU8jdxxIlGOPCxdp3G3alAZh0WMl-oPE3YFvH2ivkJJ4fA_4vt8f-wf54NPrF0Ve5cx74ncLLMJ1T7nQfeYqjWqWg0To-EvJyY4aJ9AWjN0d-XDv4-DWkxnZDryaebZ2mSb7HK71JDejY8OOjtHhPB2LdYvWZJ6OxnkZ_NrXtDXWaKPtj4d-avPECa2el5HPSY2anZdcH3-yT3LxGe78xfVx5DiE9RIpTdmfCjeFW7pLbtIjhVsfVrhpq3AzqHB75xocdESFm6-UWj_Ax5KFk0D7LJUjQ2ByXKFyYGrc4PS1CTQh4dj_6JTvuHQ5wJHri-Fi8A18giNHgoscBH4BxfLZe07hNtTVlbcPwbdpVqN-RfLhG0P-y_3Xiv8CAAD__6UwmtY) a leg amputated after being wounded in the strikes that killed his father. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israeli strikes had killed a top Iranian nuclear scientist, while Iran expanded [attacks on Gulf neighbors](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykULuSozAQ_BrIREkzssCBgkvIfOmF1BhGRrcCUWJs1n-_hX9hw35Ud3X_uw03iimuj7-0sJeQh5WPPbEIl2HNG71DLrJTyTKSCI1ftE4ygAanNCqDw0QxvQdbTz4wA2PN3rQt4tU57OrZd3eLbBk7DhYvE8O9sw4hmNDCvRtdHf2ZptGg0UbjpdGdNh04QN1eLQdXWc1TlFya_zmuMnNI7_zi0ox5qZOfRba9wj8V9BX0x3E0IX-fK069gj7FF6sTV9A_dxULrSruhTipg4pKJLyLWqiMszKgPvbnNp10Xfy0HTGluLu2svqxUEyfWvnVVy8PPwEAAP__Kn9-uQ), including Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. Also Thursday, an American KC-135 refueling tanker [went down over western](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLESnCAQhp9GOxxYFLWgSGN3aVM6KywnOQ4uwJ3j22e8PEK6nf1md_7v_3Vbb-iDj_ef-CRdXVojHSVQrZTXmF54upRrwZyqwVrRPDDaugIHxbhkQq4WfTjXvrXaEQHJlrQYRylnpeTU7loNwzwY3DaQAAPIycCME4jNWuwJeOv19Y1LIQUXXA4dn7iYQIHk49yTU03Pyfqacvc7-Vh3cuFMH8qdSc826L3WV2nkjwaWBpbjOLq4GVAXbWB5F3YZNbD4jJEdmP8tH4YJObBM7k2XP6sYH5SZyVh2KsxH5jP-YfadL_o9Ts5RLP5D1-SNx1BYwbPN2r4OH4Ivamx6fn-iD99w9b8a_Wj4GwAA__8Bi4uh) Iraq in a non-combat incident involving two aircraft, with rescue efforts underway.
## ROTC Student Kills Gunman Attacking University
An ROTC cadet ended a shooting attack by reportedly [stabbing a gunman](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF7ZMyzsFi7SuHtpU6JZPAYnxkZm3j6Rr4_IL7z6Skf3nF8f0welnMrykzZ2EutU-OvILMJtKnWnM9YmB7UqM4nQ_IdKkAkMDNqgtjgFSvmc-i64yAyMHTs7jojPYcBHtzp7D_f-HgaLFixaS5EBgx3Ny0Z8RuiSu2gGLVpjDd5v5mHsAwZAMz57joPqDYcktd1-11Rk5ZjP-uZ2m-vWZbeK7IfCHwq8Al_OvR5yTQr8BVbgDSrwFhT4z0Nffgr8yq3qy0rPFFh0JKGcT30IvV4c9NzoLwddc9ChbqmkWvTyWTYqWqreG7-5iN5qYz1TK7SwAt81F_avlHM6hlH1Ztko5f835Vtt3w7-BQAA___rE402) who opened fire inside an academic building at Old Dominion University in Norfolk, Virginia, on Thursday morning. The shooter killed an ROTC instructor and wounded two cadets before being killed. The gunman was identified as Mohamed Bailor Jalloh, 36, a former Virginia National Guardsman [previously convicted](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAQRL_GdCCz5hooXKShe2lTIl-8hs0z3iuzAfH3EfmFdCONNKNzfn3NX54S5fWn39FJ5DnjdSQUwTJn_vg7cpHDF5bFi_jl2-cgM2iwtTZ1a-bgKd1zVwUXEQFNha7te2NGa81Qbe799kMXobcjat_3PnYwYrAvE1-tBoSK3LOmTWta3WrzavSg2wEsGN2PHUarOo2BhEvzmynLhjHdfGJpFt6r5DaRz6HMDwWTgum6rmZ5Hw_F0yuYnqhg4hTqwDtl4lz_yXRiOUju-tiYhfJaZy6R03d9Ulkpk1cwVcWFz0Up0WF71el195T-3cp_uTod_A0AAP__k6t_lA) of providing material support to ISIS. The Old Dominion incident is being investigated as a terror-related attack. Later on Thursday, in an unrelated attack in Michigan, an attempted car bomber [drove a vehicle full of explosives](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOnDAQBOCnMZ1P9i6Yu4Iijbs_bUrkgzU48XmRvfefePuIvELqkT7NzK-v-SuknMr2M7xokshzoU_LJEJ1LnyEM3KVFirLEkTC8ieUVWYw4LRBbXFeQ8rn3HfrFImAsKPJjiPiwzm8d_v0DAOieZKz_YNoRBz65-isuw9xGEagLk2XZtCiNdbgcDN3Y-_gAM346Ck61Rtak3C9_eZUZKeYT_6melv41eVpFzmawh8KvAJfzoObXJECf8EKvEEF3oIC_2762qfAL6HqpYa2U9OpCOtXWva0haLbWcLG25t05Jz5Q6t-nrrtLE3HVGnV-3sjfXBOC-lK7eDSSIHv6rQen5Rzam5UvdleIeV_JeW_nv2e4G8AAAD__ymhjOw) into a West Bloomfield synagogue's front entrance before security opened fire and killed the suspect. One security guard was struck by the vehicle and hospitalized.

name: Wes Climer
subject: Character Still Matters in Public Office
body:
| | | | | |
---
| [](https://click-1930806.icptrack.com/icp/relay.php?r=12573791&msgid=19869&act=R3J4&c=1930806&pid=323727&destination=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutu.be%2FJ4aHx9A5uSw&cf=3250&v=b31b501bdce6cdca42e5b1ed9cc0efde58083204d83c5a3458ee00316b80c454)
---
| | | | One thing I hear over and over is that folks feel like government is working for the people inside it rather than the taxpayers it is supposed to serve.Government exists to serve you – not bureaucrats, not politicians, not lobbyists.Too many elected officials have lost sight of that. They treat public office as an ornament to benefit them, rather than a sacred obligation to serve others. Those entrusted with public office have a strict duty to follow the Constitution and put the interests of their constituents above their own. That conviction led me to challenge the legislative pay raise in court. Lawmakers voted to increase their own compensation by eighty percent during their current terms despite the Constitution clearly stating that legislative compensation cannot be increased during the term for which a member is elected. Many people told me the lawsuit would cost me politically, that it would impair my ability accomplish policy objectives in the legislature. They may have been right. But the principle mattered more than the politics. The South Carolina Supreme Court ultimately agreed and struck the pay raise down unanimously. The Constitution means what it says.I have tried to apply that same principle to my own service. While serving in the State Senate, I refused the legislative retirement benefit available to members. Public office should be a temporary act of service to your community and temporary public service should not confer retirement benefits. In fact, the mere existence of retirement benefits corrupts the incentives of elected officials.The same principle applies in Washington. Members of Congress should not be able to get rich from their service. They should not be able to use privileged information gained through their office for personal profit. That is why I support banning stock trading by members of Congress. Not only will I aggressively support legislation to end Congressional profiteering, I will hold myself to that standard, regardless of what the law says. I will not own individual stocks. I will not vote to raise Congressional compensation. I will not accept a Congressional pension. These issues go to the heart of whether government is serving the public or serving itself. If we want people to trust our institutions again, the people who hold office must hold themselves to a standard that earns that trust.If you believe government should work for the people it represents and not the politicians who occupy it, I would be grateful for your support.
Thank you for your support,Wes Climer

| | Peter Willis, **This is a defining moment for our country.**

Last month, President Trump delivered a powerful State of the Union address, highlighting the tremendous progress of his first year back in office and outlining a bold agenda for the year ahead.

President Trump's America First leadership is delivering real results: restoring energy dominance, securing our border, protecting Kansas communities, confronting Iran head-on to end decades of aggression, and putting hardworking Americans first.

I fully support his vision—tax cuts for working families, a stronger American economy, affordable energy, safer streets, and defeating radical policies at home and threats abroad.

[Chip in today to defend Kansas Values.](https://traceymann.us4.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60a16ea89a176679a5f31366c&id=13f23420e3&e=a9d1410029)

But Democrats are standing in the way. Their partial shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security was a dangerous political stunt—forcing essential workers without pay, halting critical operations, and risking our national security at a time when we're engaged in vital military action to protect America and our allies.

While conservatives demand accountability, fiscal responsibility, and common-sense solutions, the radical Left is determined to block progress, undermine our troops and law enforcement, and reverse our hard-won gains.

_**We're in a fight for the soul of America. If the Left prevails, their socialist ideals will erode freedom, faith, personal responsibility, and opportunity—while emboldening enemies abroad.**_

This movement is about preserving the values that built this nation and keeping America the land of promise, not government overreach or weakness.

The other side won't stop. They're raising millions, weaponizing government, and working to silence us and derail President Trump's agenda—including our strong stand with Israel.

**We can't let them.**

Will you [chip in today](https://traceymann.us4.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60a16ea89a176679a5f31366c&id=9c4ff46dda&e=a9d1410029), before the end of the quarter, to stand with us? Every dollar fuels the pressure to expand our conservative majority, defend President Trump's priorities, support our troops in the fight, and continue to take our conservative Kansas values to DC.

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

Trump just declared all-out war on our voting rights – and our democracy.

As part of his plan to rig the midterms, Trump is demanding Senate
Republicans bulldoze Senate rules and abolish the filibuster to ram
through the so-called “SAVE Act” NEXT WEEK – a scheme that could silence
21 million Americans and rip away our freedom to vote.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36186?source=email-20260313&t=1017&akid=10380%2E5885482%2Ew820UA ]Headline: Trump-backed SAVE America Act will get a Senate vote next
week, Thune says

The bill already passed the House, and now Trump is ramping up his threats
to force it through the Senate – vowing not to sign a single piece of
legislation until Congress bows to his demands. If we don’t act, he could
grind our government to a halt until Senate Majority Leader Thune caves
and guts voting rights nationwide.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36186?source=email-20260313&t=1018&akid=10380%2E5885482%2Ew820UA ]We have to show MASSIVE public pressure on the Senate to stand up to
Trump and stop this. Take urgent action: tell your senator “Vote NO on the
SAVE Act NOW!”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36186?source=email-20260313&t=1019&akid=10380%2E5885482%2Ew820UA ]ADD YOUR NAME

Here’s what’s at stake: if Trump gets his way, every American would need
to present a passport or birth certificate just to register to vote – and
a photo ID every time they cast a ballot. But 1-in-10 eligible voters
don’t have up-to-date documents – disenfranchising MILLIONS overnight. And
that’s not even all – it would also require states to run voter rolls
through a federal database kept by the Department of Homeland Security.

It’s no accident: Trump’s scheme is designed to purge the rolls and keep
our communities from having a voice.

And the scary thing is that Trump’s threats are working. Texas Senator
Cornyn, who is locked in a tight primary race, just reversed himself and
came out in favor of abandoning the filibuster after YEARS of unflinching
support for it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36186?source=email-20260313&t=1020&akid=10380%2E5885482%2Ew820UA ]Headline: Sen. John Cornyn flips on the filibuster to pass SAVE America
Act as Trump weighs endorsement

If we don’t speak out, more Senators could flip. We can’t stay silent
while Trump and his enablers try to snatch our rights away. As Trump
escalates his pressure campaign, Congress needs to hear from all of us –
not tomorrow, today.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36186?source=email-20260313&t=1021&akid=10380%2E5885482%2Ew820UA ]Add your name now and tell your senators: Don’t cave to Trump – vote NO
on the SAVE Act!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36186?source=email-20260313&t=1022&akid=10380%2E5885482%2Ew820UA ]ADD YOUR NAME

Let’s rise up and show Congress that we won’t let any politician – no
matter how powerful – slam the door on our democracy.

When we organize, we win,

Our Revolution

name: NEGOP
subject: 🚨 Your Weekly Update From The NEGOP
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nebraska Republican Party 1610 N St
body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
The filing deadline has passed, and the candidate lineup for Nebraska's May 12 primary is now set. With challenges and credentialing wrapping up soon, the stage is fully prepared for what promises to be a pivotal election--just two short months away.
Voter turnout will decide the outcome. Republicans boast a strong slate of candidates across the board, but victories depend entirely on our supporters showing up at the polls. Apathy is not an option in 2026. Our focus at NEGOP is clear: deliver sharp, motivating messaging, drive high turnout, and provide full support to every Republican candidate. We're all in to help them succeed.
In parallel over the next four weeks, County parties will be holding county conventions. An energized base will go about the business of electing new officers in some cases as well as delegates and alternates to then represent them at the State Convention. Some counties, previously inactive, will form county party structures.
Preparations are ramping up for the 2026 Nebraska Republican State Convention on Saturday, June 6 in Congressional District 2. This is more than an event--it's a launchpad for victory.
We're securing dynamic speakers and finalizing a robust agenda. The 2nd Annual Vote Red Auction will cap off Friday, June 5, with a special dinner and entertainment. Delegates, alternates, guests, candidates, officeholders, speakers, and vendors will come together for collaboration, networking, and strategy sessions.
Expect idea-sharing, election-winning tactics, emphasis on building strong county parties, and a clear call to put mission above position. This convention will energize our team and equip us to win in November.
We're actively recruiting volunteers and sponsors to ensure the experience is enjoyable, educational, and impactful for everyone involved.
Your support makes this possible. Consider becoming a sponsor of the convention or signing up as a recurring monthly donor to NEGOP. The more our fellow Republicans invest, the more we can invest in candidates, turnout efforts, and building a stronger party.
Let's turn energy into votes--together. Stay tuned for more convention details; and thank you for your commitment to Nebraska's Republican future.
Together we win.
For Nebraska, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair The filing deadline has passed, and the candidate lineup for Nebraska's May 12 primary is now set. With challenges and credentialing wrapping up soon, the stage is fully prepared for what promises to be a pivotal election--just two short months away. Voter turnout will decide the outcome. Republicans boast a strong slate of candidates across the board, but victories depend entirely on our supporters showing up at the polls. Apathy is not an option in 2026. Our focus at NEGOP is clear: deliver sharp, motivating messaging, drive high turnout, and provide full support to every Republican candidate. We're all in to help them succeed. In parallel over the next four weeks, County parties will be holding county conventions. An energized base will go about the business of electing new officers in some cases as well as delegates and alternates to then represent them at the State Convention. Some counties, previously inactive, will form county party structures. Preparations are ramping up for the 2026 Nebraska Republican State Convention on Saturday, June 6 in Congressional District 2. This is more than an event--it's a launchpad for victory. We're securing dynamic speakers and finalizing a robust agenda. The 2nd Annual Vote Red Auction will cap off Friday, June 5, with a special dinner and entertainment. Delegates, alternates, guests, candidates, officeholders, speakers, and vendors will come together for collaboration, networking, and strategy sessions. Expect idea-sharing, election-winning tactics, emphasis on building strong county parties, and a clear call to put mission above position. This convention will energize our team and equip us to win in November. We're actively recruiting volunteers and sponsors to ensure the experience is enjoyable, educational, and impactful for everyone involved. Your support makes this possible. Consider becoming a sponsor of the convention or signing up as a recurring monthly donor to NEGOP. The more our fellow Republicans invest, the more we can invest in candidates, turnout efforts, and building a stronger party. Let's turn energy into votes--together. Stay tuned for more convention details; and thank you for your commitment to Nebraska's Republican future. Together we win. If our opponents are willing to sell out our environment to win this race, what other values will they fold on?
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40972%2E3422442%2EWkbRI2)
Peter,
When it comes to protecting our environment from fossil fuel polluters, there’s a huge difference between the candidates running for California governor. **Katie Porter is the only leading candidate in this race who has never cashed a check or made a dollar from Big Oil.**
Eric Swalwell just took the maximum contribution possible—nearly $40,000—from an oil company, _despite signing a public pledge to not take fossil fuel money._
And Tom Steyer made his billions by investing in Big Oil and other polluters.
If our opponents are willing to sell out our environment to win this race, what other values will they fold on?
With Donald Trump declaring open season for new offshore drilling in California waters, we need a governor who is not beholden to Big Oil. A governor who has always taken them on. That’s Katie Porter.
Her campaign is funded by grassroots donations so you can be sure she will fight for working families, not corporate or billionaire interests. She doesn’t take money from corporations or corporate PACs and never will.
But here’s the problem: our opponents could have a financial edge from their dirty oil money. So Katie’s counting on Porter Supporters like you, Peter, to help her fight back.

## Arlington Hosts IndyCar Grand Prix
IndyCar is [coming to North Texas](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb2uqzoQRp8Guon8FxsKitvQ7dueEg32OLFC7MieHcLbH5FXOOXok5a01vz5WX4wbSnf_scnTfyJZcm0t42YqS63ijm8avqs1DjTXqkx_lbMixLKgtAg9RIwbcdi-jCtIoyyp0k6p41wygz9fYre4BrUdXUD2uj86PU6GKesGxxJHPs0nTChpZZaODlenLxGa4WMJEdtY-iMoJC41AvfiemDLW5HeVO9-PLst-nO_Gqd_q9Tc6fmfd8ve0Q8x07NWDn5jTo1U2aqjCk_KfN5v6kefE_5Bkf5hUwUgAs8ctnhq5dyODxW-FaAMwNgPVtxycDJP4gb-JI9VW7n7qnBC-vjRMZSQqdmNTgwpJUNKoJWowNj4goj0gro7eqdJXHVtq9TeO1p21KzrjPi9sS0ff34377yntTfAAAA__86X6Mx) this weekend for the inaugural Java House Grand Prix of Arlington. During the premiere event on Sunday, 25 drivers will do 70 laps around AT&T Stadium and Globe Life Field on a 2.73-mile course. The weekend also features races in the Toyota GR Cup and USF Pro 2000 series, [several stunt shows](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSpCAQhJ8GMy0YPHADgkvM9tILrVEGpQrRgtl19-2vvFf4867u_r6_z-mJMcW8_sGdHH_CMWW6aiJmKtNaMPuzxM9MlTNdhSrjq2CeQIJppW6VnjzG9J36xrtZ-odqyClrdS8t9EOzOWvnQS1GYT941AghSIkBIQxgZg9zE91dJrXSSkurHp1Vv4IxUgVSD22CF70kH_koHW_E9MEa0vd4U-mWY2-S25jPKvRvAaOA8bqubj2x3FB85DsjYKQ3ZW5jDoeAsS4b-VciAWMo0eO33bEsW6t0e19pivPnFVOK1VjRy3XHmP5v8c8MvR38CwAA__9Cdntr) each day, and daily live performances. Several former Cowboys and Rangers players will be on hand to sign autographs, including Charles Haley, Drew Pearson, Elvis Andrus, and Ivan “Pudge” Rodriguez. Work on the venue [started](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L_OozAQBPCnMR3IfwjgwsU1dLn2SrSwa2LJsaO1Ccnbn_he4atHGs38_t2XO4QY0v4XnuTqx-cl0Vki1Uq87AwJXxw-K5Wa6GQqFQ6GtGiph1aaVpkFIcTv0jfoVolWNeTUOJpejrqfmofzWiFatSJaMyltxwlWv94220vtJQ1NcFeZNMooI0dlu1Hd_DBI5UlZM3gUvSQMNXNXH1TpA8XHb34Td1t-NtE9an0VYf4IPQs9n-fZpXVDf16x0PP1R-g55g2i0DNnwHaLuRxMpQ0Jjv1giC3wxVBzakPC7wbcMmwk9Gys7ScrhZ4bdvg6Q4yhDKPo5f6EEH9G1N_RvZ3-HwAA__9174P3) months ago. First responders will be stationed at each of the course's 14 turns, and a fully operational medical center has been set up behind the grandstands. body:
The federally funded smear campaign just went live. Here’s my response.
[View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e1030561/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvMmtteFpNYnROQg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMTM/LbmNsMURvaGFQUA/qP2hpZHM9bmNsNEdGZEREdDZRQXZscw/gabQPrg/s7jbc2bc351)

| Dear Friend,
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-harder-hitting-hf?utm_source=lg-omg-harder-hitting&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=25") They came for me **with your tax dollars.** This week, NPR — a news network that runs on federal funding — aired a hit piece designed to do one thing: build the public case that what I do should be illegal. They called my journalism **“slimy.”** They called it **“sleazy.”** They gave a lawyer airtime to describe my reporting the same way a mob boss describes a cop who got too close. **Not a single person on that broadcast could challenge what’s on tape.** **[**DONATE $35 — Fight back right now →**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-harder-hitting-hf?utm_source=lg-omg-harder-hitting&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=25")** Here’s what’s on tape: A Department of Homeland Security employee — on a date he thought was private — told a woman he’d just met exactly what he thought of the people Americans elected to run their government. That video has been seen by **2.5 million people.** His boss put him on leave. Then fired him. **Now he’s suing me.** And he’s not alone. Men captured on camera across **DHS, the Secret Service, and the FBI** are testing every legal theory their lawyers can dream up — fraud, invasion of privacy, you name it. The lawsuits aren’t designed to win. **They’re designed to make the cost of this journalism unbearable.** **[**DONATE $50 — Cover a First Amendment defense motion →**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-harder-hitting-hf?utm_source=lg-omg-harder-hitting&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=25")** **This is the playbook.** Discredit the journalist. Amplify the lawsuits. Make running a camera expensive enough that nobody ever does it again. NPR just ran chapter one. My attorney told them I was too busy working on the next story to comment. That’s true. But I’ll be honest with you, **Patriot** : staying too busy to comment requires resources I’m burning through fast. **Every court filing costs money.** Every deposition costs money. Every hour my legal team spends keeping these cameras in the field costs money. **[**DONATE $150 — Keep an investigation running for one more week →**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-harder-hitting-hf?utm_source=lg-omg-harder-hitting&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=25")** Here’s what they can’t take from me: **the fact that this works.** The men on those videos are not anonymous. The agencies they work for are not faceless. The contempt they showed for elected leadership — for **you** , Patriot — is now part of the permanent record. Two and a half million people watched it. NPR covered it because **they had no choice.** **You don’t run a federally funded hit piece on a journalist unless his work is landing.** Liberty Guard has set up my legal defense fund to make sure it **keeps** landing. Every dollar you give goes directly to the legal fight — not overhead, not consultants. **The fight.** **[**DONATE $500 — Become a Founding Defender of this work →**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-harder-hitting-hf?utm_source=lg-omg-harder-hitting&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=25")** **They think if they make this painful enough, I’ll stop.** **They don’t know you.** **[**STAND WITH JAMES — Donate Now →**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/liberty-guard/lg-omg-harder-hitting-hf?utm_source=lg-omg-harder-hitting&utm_medium=hf&utm_campaign=mb&amount=25")** In Truth,
James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

Hi Peter, Last month, the Trump EPA revoked the bedrock scientific ruling that allows the government to regulate greenhouse gas pollution: the Endangerment Finding. It reminded me of when 14 inches of rain fell on Southeast Wisconsin in 24 hours last summer, causing more than $22 million in damage to public infrastructure. In the wake of these devastating floods, we applied for FEMA disaster aid to help repair the public infrastructure: roads, storm systems, the things our whole community depends on. We made the case. We appealed twice. **The Trump administration said no.** This is not a coincidence. This is the MAGA governing philosophy: Let communities like ours bear the brunt of climate change, while removing regulations for the fossil fuel industry and polluters. I have spent nearly six years as Milwaukee County Executive fighting to get our communities what they need: balanced budgets, new housing, cleaner air, safer streets. And I've learned that when Washington fails to show up, local leaders have to fight twice as hard. **As Governor, I will show up for every community that gets left behind by this administration.** I will build a Wisconsin that invests in climate mitigation, clean infrastructure, and the climate action that creates jobs and lowers costs — because I've already done it. **We cut Milwaukee County's carbon emissions by nearly 50%. We invested in smarter, more resilient infrastructure. | | Friend,
**Isaiah 62:6 says,**_**"I have posted watchmen on your walls, O Jerusalem; they will never be silent day or night."**_
A watchman doesn't wait to be asked. He doesn't look around to see if someone else will do it. He stands at his post, eyes open, voice ready, because the alternative is unthinkable.
**I believe that is exactly where we are in America right now, and I am not willing to be silent.**
As Kentucky's Attorney General, I stood watch. **I fought COVID** vaccine mandates and won. **I protected children** from irreversible gender procedures. **I defended law enforcement** when radicals surrounded my home chanting “burn it down.”
I did not flinch. I did not negotiate. I did not go silent.
**That is the record and the spirit I will bring to the U.S. Senate.**
Because here’s what I know: the Left wants this seat badly. They are organized, they are funded, and they are counting on people of faith to decide that someone else will handle it.
**But watchmen don't do that. Watchmen stay at their post.**

clean_body: | | | | | | | Friend, Isaiah 62:6 says,"I have posted watchmen on your walls, O Jerusalem; they will never be silent day or night." A watchman doesn't wait to be asked. He doesn't look around to see if someone else will do it. He stands at his post, eyes open, voice ready, because the alternative is unthinkable. I believe that is exactly where we are in America right now, and I am not willing to be silent. As Kentucky's Attorney General, I stood watch. I fought COVID vaccine mandates and won. I protected children from irreversible gender procedures. I defended law enforcement when radicals surrounded my home chanting “burn it down.” I did not flinch. I did not negotiate. I did not go silent. That is the record and the spirit I will bring to the U.S. Senate. Because here’s what I know: the Left wants this seat badly. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: Why the Iran Conflict Could Hurt Private Credit Next
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
Since the U.S. and Israel struck Iran on February 28, the S&P 500 has held up surprisingly well, falling only about 1.5%. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/08/stock-market-today-live-updates.html] Oil briefly surged past $120 a barrel [https://www.reuters.com/business/sterling-slumps-oils-surge-120-iran-war-rocks-markets-2026-03-09/] before coming down below $100.
Wall Street’s collective posture has largely been that this is a short-term interruption, not a long war but closing out last night all three major US benchmarks finished at their lowest closing levels of 2026 [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-futures-inch-up-after-stocks-sink-to-lowest-levels-since-november-225332831.html] — and at their lowest points since November. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped over 700 points [https://abcnews.com/Business/oil-prices-surge-stocks-fall-iran-escalates-shipping/story?id=130995443] , closing below 47,000 for the first time this year.
Many folks in the White House are saying the war is over - that we already won. I served in Baghdad with the 82nd Airborne in 2003. I remember when we were told the operation would be over in months. Instead, it lasted eight years and cost $3+ trillion. The markets weren't pricing in that outcome either.
Don’t get me wrong, people should be stoic in their Wall Street market investments, but I could do without the bravado from the DC politicians who’ve never seen combat.
As Scott Galloway writes in his latest newsletter [https://www.profgmedia.com/p/are-markets-wrong-about-iran] , “Three-quarters of conflicts since World War II ended with stocks in the green a year later, so the market’s reaction to this makes sense on paper. What strikes me is investors’ conviction that this doesn’t change much. Steve Eisman, the investor who predicted the 2008 crash, told me this doesn’t change his investment strategy by a single dollar. I’m hearing that everywhere. No one is willing to contend with the downside scenarios. What if Iran is destabilized even further?”
Why Private Credit Could Be Impacted By Iran
When geopolitics face a shockwave, everyone watches stock and oil prices. But there's a less visible market that deserves equal attention where the damage could be far more consequential: private credit.
Private credit is a $2 trillion market [https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/blue-owl-turmoil-adds-strain-2-trillion-us-private-credit-sector-2026-02-27/] that most Americans are unaware of. In simple terms, it's when investment firms — not banks — lend money directly to companies. Instead of a business going to JPMorgan for a loan - the biggest bank in the world - it goes to Blackstone, Apollo, or Blue Owl, typically at higher interest rates and with more flexible terms. Pension funds, university endowments, and sovereign wealth funds are among the largest investors in these funds.
Companies turn to private credit when they need speed, discretion, or flexibility that traditional banks won't offer – a fast acquisition, a turnaround situation, or a deal too complex for standard underwriting
Here's where Iran makes an already stressed system worse. Almost every private credit loan has a floating interest rate [https://www.morganstanley.com/ideas/private-credit-outlook-considerations] . As inflation expectations rise and Treasury yields climb (they jumped 20 basis points [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-10-year-treasury-yield-forecast-only-gently-drift-up-following-war-surge-2026-03-11/] in a single week after the Iranian strikes), every borrower in every private credit portfolio automatically owes more on their loan. The most vulnerable borrowers are mid-sized manufacturers, logistics firms, and software companies — businesses where a simultaneous jump in energy costs and debt payments can be the difference between making payroll and missing a loan payment
Private credit already had a problem before Iran. UBS researchers estimated this month that up to 35% of private credit portfolios carry elevated risk from AI disruption [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/03/private-credit-stocks-plummet-on-concern-about-exposure-to-software-industry-disrupted-by-ai.html] . Iran adds a second layer: if geopolitical instability triggers a broader market downturn, those same companies face both a structural threat from AI and a macroeconomic headwind simultaneously.
The Gulf States Role in American Private Credit
The Gulf states — UAE [https://www.institutionalinvestor.com/article/abu-dhabi-moves-become-gulfs-private-credit-capital] , Saudi Arabia [https://www.reuters.com/markets/asia/saudi-arabias-pif-strikes-multi-billion-investment-deals-with-us-asset-managers-2025-05-14/] , Qatar [https://www.qia.qa/en/Newsroom/Pages/Qatar-Investment-Authority-and-Goldman-Sachs-Sign-MoU-to-Expand-Strategic-Partnership-with-$25bn-Investment-Target.aspx] , Bahrain [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/bahrain-us-private-firms-sign-17-billion-worth-agreements-says-court-bahraini-2025-07-16/] , Kuwait [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-10-27/goldman-vies-for-10-billion-from-kuwait-in-private-funds-push] — were countries attacked by Iran these last 13 days and each of these countries have a significant role to play in U.S. private credit. Through their massive sovereign wealth funds, they are among the largest investors in American private credit and private equity. They are, in the language of the industry, limited partners (LPs) — the money behind the money.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/chart.png]
According to Forbes [https://www.forbes.com/sites/mayrarodriguezvalladares/2026/03/07/should-we-worry-about-gulf-countries-reducing-investments-in-the-us/] , these six countries invest roughly $2 trillion in the U.S., representing over 35% of their total assets under management. Their $420 billion stake in U.S. private equity alone accounts for 8-10% of the entire market — outsized influence for nations whose combined population is roughly the size of California and Texas.
Iran's missiles landing on Gulf soil changes the calculus. These strikes were a direct consequence of U.S. military action, which means the funds bankrolling American private markets are now weighing their exposure against a conflict that America and Israel started.
Whether these funds pull back from U.S. private markets, redeploy capital toward defense spending at home, or start using their LP positions as leverage in broader geopolitical negotiations is an open question. The answer could show up in American private credit portfolios before most investors even know to look for it.
Private credit is projected to reach $5 trillion by 2029, according to Morgan Stanley [https://www.morganstanley.com/ideas/private-credit-outlook-considerations] . It is no longer a niche corner of finance, but a structural pillar of how American companies borrow money. If the Gulf sovereign wealth funds start pulling back their investments, the ramifications could be devastating for U.S. businesses that rely on them. Borrowing costs rise and deals wouldn’t get done.
What’s happening in Iran isn’t just about some war happening across the globe. It’s also a story of how a whole network of countries are connected through shared business interests.
Appreciate you reading our newsletter. We had a great week being quoted in Bloomberg [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-03-08/green-investors-told-to-sit-tight-through-war-fueled-turmoil?embedded-checkout=true] , CNBC [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/03/06/iran-war-data-centers.html] and other outlets. Be sure to follow me on Instagram [https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124844072/599887666/-513936443?hl=en&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDYyMjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWQxNmY0OTUtNmMwMy1mMTExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJwZXRlcmZveDEwMjJAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nvBZs1pDhprrRo8w9hGkaNJ33BW9iySnZIIvooLBYQk=&emci=6a6c850a-ec02-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=9d16f495-6c03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=20196921] and subscribe to my Substack [https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124844077/599887671/-2141829100?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDYyMjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWQxNmY0OTUtNmMwMy1mMTExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJwZXRlcmZveDEwMjJAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nvBZs1pDhprrRo8w9hGkaNJ33BW9iySnZIIvooLBYQk=&emci=6a6c850a-ec02-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=9d16f495-6c03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=20196921] for my weekly geopolitical and business analysis. Please keep our troops and that region in your prayers.
-Patrick

President Donald Trump **[stopped everything during his rally](https://substack.com/redirect/6b2c69fe-f0c9-49ae-9125-7fcdae27e481?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Kentucky when a supporter in the crowd collapsed. What happened next was nothing short of a miracle.
"Is there a doctor in the house?! Take your time..."

# **[The 1970s Called. Stagflation Is Back. Gold Went Up 2,000% Last Time](https://substack.com/redirect/9185cd15-d5a7-4a53-b806-faa1663820d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ...**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9185cd15-d5a7-4a53-b806-faa1663820d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The last time America faced stagflation -- inflation running hot while the economy slowed -- it was the 1970s. Gold went up over 2,000%.
Here's what's happening right now: U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz -- the chokepoint for 20% of the world's oil. Brent crude spiked 13% in a single session. Oil is now up roughly 74% in three weeks.
The Fed is now trapped. Cut rates and inflation accelerates. Hold rates and the economy slows. That's the stagflation box -- and it's exactly the environment gold was built for.
The S&P 500 is negative on the year. Gold is up 22%. JPMorgan's 2026 target is $6,300, with an upside case of $8,500 if the conflict prolongs.
Most retirement accounts are 95%+ in stocks and bonds -- the two assets hit hardest when inflation and slow growth arrive together.
**[See what the Iran war, oil shock, and stagflation risk mean for a stock-heavy IRA here.](https://substack.com/redirect/9185cd15-d5a7-4a53-b806-faa1663820d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

That's what rats do" and that new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is "wounded and likely disfigured." Hegseth noted Khamenei failed to appear in person when his first statement since being appointed was read on Iranian state TV Thursday, asking "Iran has plenty of cameras and plenty of voice recorders. Why a written statement? I think you know why?"

* **Why it matters:** Khamenei has not been seen or heard publicly since US-Israeli strikes on Feb. 28 killed his father, wife and other family members, leading to speculation about his whereabouts and health. President Trump speculated Thursday that Khamenei was "probably alive" but may have been wounded during Operation Epic Fury, while one source told The Sun the supreme leader was in a coma. Experts suggest Khamenei's read-out message indicates he is "little more than a figurehead within the regime" with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps remaining "the real center of power."

# **Trump vows fresh wave of deadly attacks on Iran 's "deranged scumbags" after two US terror attacks**
### _" Watch what happens to these deranged scumbags today."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22af90fa-0527-4b05-8a7f-ca78d7237af4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
President Donald Trump **[issued a new threat against Iran's leadership](https://substack.com/redirect/22af90fa-0527-4b05-8a7f-ca78d7237af4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** early Friday, vowing to use his "unparalleled firepower" for fresh deadly strikes after new Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei delivered his first public remarks and two extremists attacked a synagogue and college in the US Thursday. Trump wrote on Truth Social that "Iran's Navy is gone, their Air Force is no longer, missiles, drones and everything else are being decimated, and their leaders have been wiped from the face of the earth," warning "watch what happens to these deranged scumbags today."
* **Why it matters:** Khamenei's inaugural speech called for the Islamic Republic to "obtain compensation" from enemies or "destroy its assets to the same extent," with experts believing the address was used to activate Iranian sleeper cells abroad to commit attacks. Law enforcement agencies worldwide remain on heightened alert, with Trump boasting the US military has "unparalleled firepower, unlimited ammunition, and plenty of time," adding "they've been killing innocent people all over the world for 47 years, and now I, as the 47th President of the United States of America, am killing them."
* **The attacks:** On Thursday, convicted ISIS terrorist Mohamed Bailor Jalloh allegedly shouted "Allahu Akbar" before opening fire inside an Old Dominion University classroom, killing decorated Lt. Col. Brandon Shah, chair of the military science department who had served tours in Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation Enduring Freedom. Separately, 41-year-old Lebanese-native Ayman Mohamad Ghazali rammed an explosives-filled car loaded with mortar shells into Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Michigan, before the temple's security opened fire, killing him--Ghazali had at least four relatives, including a sibling, killed days earlier in Israeli strikes against Hezbollah targets in Beirut. The Israeli military announced it launched a "wide-scale wave of strikes" across Iran Friday targeting underground missile facilities, aerial defense bases and command centers.

* * *
# **Old Dominion shooter ID 'd as Mohamed Bailor Jalloh, former National Guard soldier previously convicted of supporting ISIS**
Mohamed Bailor Jalloh, 36, **[a former National Guard soldier previously convicted of supporting ISIS,](https://substack.com/redirect/22dbe591-b2b4-42b0-a182-85936881c36f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** has been identified as the Old Dominion University gunman who stormed into an ROTC classroom Thursday and fatally shot a retired military officer before a heroic student stabbed him to death. Jalloh was sentenced to 11 years in prison and five years of supervised release but was let out early in December 2024, according to the New York Post.
* **Why it matters:** Jalloh discussed plans to carry out a "Fort Hood-style attack" with a government informant he believed was an ISIS terrorist, traveled to Africa in 2015 to meet with an ISIS recruiter, and even boarded a truck full of terror recruits in Niger before bailing after 18 hours. He praised the Chattanooga gunman who killed five soldiers in 2015 and sent $500 to a man he believed was an ISIS member who was actually an undercover FBI agent, pleading guilty in October 2015 to attempting to provide material support to ISIS.
* **What happened:** FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed one person is dead and two others wounded, saying "the shooter is now deceased thanks to a group of brave students who stepped in and subdued him - actions that undoubtedly saved lives along with the quick response of law enforcement." The FBI is investigating as an act of terrorism, with Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll saying the injured victims were "Army personnel." The shooting occurred hours before an attacker rammed a vehicle into a Michigan synagogue and opened fire.

* * *
# **Minnesota 's paid leave law faces fraud concerns just two months after taking effect under Gov. Tim Walz**
Minnesota's **[paid leave legislation,](https://substack.com/redirect/10e7c19b-8267-493d-ad53-a85ae1b88a10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** which took effect January 1 and allows workers up to 12 weeks off with partial pay for family care and up to 12 weeks for personal illness (capped at 20 weeks total), is already receiving pushback over abuse concerns. The Minnesota Chamber of Commerce reports "providers are being pressured by patients for the full 12 weeks of leave, even if their condition does not require it" and "employees are going on vacation or to music festivals while supposedly on leave."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/10e7c19b-8267-493d-ad53-a85ae1b88a10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** State Sen. Michael Holmstrom said a major employer in his district has seen a 700% increase in paid leave usage since the law took effect, unable to backfill positions with skilled workers, resulting in "carrying on with business as usual without replacements and providing a lower level of service." State Sen. Mark Koran warned "the liberal use guidelines mean employees can take a day off every week, or every Monday and Friday for a long weekend," predicting the law will result in "fewer jobs, lower pay, decreased benefits and a continued exodus of business creation."
* **The oversight concerns:** The program is enforced by the Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development with over 400 full-time employees, causing uneasiness given the "multiple state agency bureaucracies that oversaw the massive fraud scandal" in Minnesota. Critics warned it could be the "next billion-dollar fraud," with policy fellow Bill Glahn saying "when you build a multibillion-dollar state benefit program with weak oversight, fraudsters line up." A department spokesperson defended the program, noting Minnesota is "one of 13 states, plus the District of Columbia" with such a program and that they "take program integrity seriously."

I’m going to say something that might shock you: The Senate just passed a bill that will help families afford housing. You read that right, Democrats and Republicans came together to get something done for the American people. The bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act I introduced with Senator Scott just passed the Senate 89 to 10. It includes more than 40 different provisions to help bring housing costs down, boost supply, reduce homelessness, cut red tape and streamline construction, expand access to homeownership, and increase oversight and efficiency of federal housing programs. **This is the largest housing bill that has been passed in 30 years. Year after year Congress has stood by and been shocked at the rising cost of housing. Now we’re actually doing something about it — and showing what’s possible when our government actually works for working people.** [**I’m going to fight my heart out to help Democrats take back our majorities this November. But even with Republicans controlling Congress, there are still some places where the door is open to making real change — and I’m going to fight to get as much done as possible with the Congress we have now. Will you pitch in $28 or anything you can now to strengthen our fight?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3502?amount=28&t=8&akid=2814%2E4032634%2EQpWMIt)

We are in a dire housing crisis across rural communities, small towns, suburban neighborhoods, and major cities. A majority of Americans can’t afford rent on a modest 2 bedroom. Nearly two in three renters don’t believe they could buy a home in the foreseeable future. Americans aren't buying their first home until 40 — while hearing stories of their grandparents buying their home for a handful of peanuts. Since 1990, the cost of housing is up 174% while wages have flatlined. This is a simple Economics 101 problem: We’ve got to increase the supply of available housing on the market to bring down costs. We do that in this bill by cutting bureaucratic red tape, expanding access to homeownership, making robust federal investments to build more housing that families want to live in, and preventing private equity executives from hoarding homes as investment opportunities that should be owned and lived in by families. **The House should pass this bill immediately so we can lower housing costs for families across the country. If they do not, they will have to explain to families across the country in November why they refused to lower the cost of housing.** [**I’m going to keep doing everything I can to get this bill passed, work with the Congress we have now to get relief to the American people, and take back our majorities in November so we can pass more transformational policies for working people. clean_body: | | | I’m going to say something that might shock you: The Senate just passed a bill that will help families afford housing. You read that right, Democrats and Republicans came together to get something done for the American people. The bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act I introduced with Senator Scott just passed the Senate 89 to 10. It includes more than 40 different provisions to help bring housing costs down, boost supply, reduce homelessness, cut red tape and streamline construction, expand access to homeownership, and increase oversight and efficiency of federal housing programs. This is the largest housing bill that has been passed in 30 years. Year after year Congress has stood by and been shocked at the rising cost of housing. Now we’re actually doing something about it — and showing what’s possible when our government actually works for working people. If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically: | | | | | | | We are in a dire housing crisis across rural communities, small towns, suburban neighborhoods, and major cities. A majority of Americans can’t afford rent on a modest 2 bedroom. Nearly two in three renters don’t believe they could buy a home in the foreseeable future. Americans aren't buying their first home until 40 — while hearing stories of their grandparents buying their home for a handful of peanuts. Since 1990, the cost of housing is up 174% while wages have flatlined. This is a simple Economics 101 problem: We’ve got to increase the supply of available housing on the market to bring down costs. We do that in this bill by cutting bureaucratic red tape, expanding access to homeownership, making robust federal investments to build more housing that families want to live in, and preventing private equity executives from hoarding homes as investment opportunities that should be owned and lived in by families. The House should pass this bill immediately so we can lower housing costs for families across the country. If they do not, they will have to explain to families across the country in November why they refused to lower the cost of housing. # The Latest from the Campaign Trail
---
|
---
|

| | | | | | | | | | | |

**California Democratic Convention**

We attended the California Democratic Convention from February 20 to February 22, 2026. The team had a busy but successful weekend as Tessa was endorsed by both the California Democratic Party and California Young Democrats. Tessa was one of the few candidates anywhere on the ballot to receive the CADEM endorsement, let alone be dual endorsed by both CADEM and CYD.
---

**Recent Endorsements**
Besides the**California Democratic Party** and**California Young Democrats,** we’ve received recent endorsements from:
**UFCW 1167** – United Food and Commercial Workers International Union
**Nichelle Henderson, candidate for California Superintendent of Public Instruction**
**Clarissa Cervantes, Riverside City Council Member** "I am honored to give my full support and endorsement to Tessa Lynn Hodge, a person who will show up and fight for the residents of CA Congressional District 23. Tessa and I share a common agenda to ensure the Constitution is respected and the rule of law is upheld, regardless of race, religion, or party– and no matter who occupies the seats of power in this country. For Tessa, “People over Party” is so much more than a slogan–it’s a promise."
**Assemblymember John Harabedian, California State Assembly District 41** "I'm proud to endorse Tessa Lynn Hodge for Congress. We need local, homegrown leaders like her in Washington D.C. who are going to fight to lower costs across California, invest in our communities, and stand up for working families. Tessa knows what it takes to get things done and I hope you'll join me in supporting Tessa Lynn Hodge for Congress District 23!"
**Seta Ghazarian, President, High Desert Progressive Democrats** “As President of the High Desert Progressive Democrats, I’m proud to endorse Tessa Lynn Hodge for Congress in California’s 23rd District. Tessa understands the realities of life in the High Desert, such as rising costs, access to quality healthcare, and the importance of small businesses to our local economy. She listens, she shows up, and she leads with heart. Tessa will be a strong voice for our communities and will bring integrity and accountability to Washington.”

Hey folks,
I jumped on a quick live with **Adam Mockler** and we covered a lot in about twenty minutes -- war, lies, media consolidation, and why independent voices matter more than ever. We talked about the horrific school bombing in Iran, the complete lack of accountability in Washington, and why the media landscape is about to change in a big way.
**Here are a few moments you don 't want to miss from the recording:**
* **00:01:07** The conversation opens with the devastating school bombing in Iran -- early reporting suggests a U.S. Tomahawk missile may have hit a girls' school, killing more than a hundred children, while the administration scrambles to deny responsibility.
* **00:04:47** Adam breaks down what he calls the administration's "transparency crisis" -- from war messaging to investigations that mysteriously disappear when they get too close to powerful people.
* **00:08:10** I respond to Bill O'Reilly attacking younger Americans as the "earbuds generation" and explain why people won't sacrifice for a country that no longer feels like it's fighting for them.
* **00:15:00** We dig into the culture of pardons and impunity in Trump-world -- and why so many officials seem convinced they'll never be held accountable for anything.
* **00:21:05** We wrap on the looming Warner Bros. media merger and why independent media -- the kind you're supporting here -- is becoming more important than ever.

This episode is about more than one war or one scandal. It's about a pattern: leaders who lie, institutions that refuse to hold anyone accountable, and a media ecosystem that's increasingly controlled by a handful of powerful interests. Conversations like this are why independent media matters -- because if we don't build our own platforms, someone else will decide what the truth looks like. If you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.
