HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031326_1&amount=25]
Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.
Team, Every voter needs to know about this massive change. Will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about the USPS changes so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031326_1&amount=35]

We're worried about every mail-in voter getting their ballot in on time, but especially those most vulnerable to this change, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home. None of them deserve to be disenfranchised from our elections over DOGE's cost-cutting measures.
Whether you can fuel our work today or not, we appreciate your support and we hope you can spread the word about this USPS change to your friends, family, and colleagues. You never know how a quick mention of something like this news might truly impact someone else's life.
Thank you,

Dear Friend, Across the country this week, state Freedom Caucus members were fighting bloated budgets, exposing big-government Republicans, pushing tax relief, and defending constitutional rights.In many state capitols, the biggest fight is not between Republicans and Democrats. It is between conservatives and the **Uniparty** **RINOs** who protect bigger government. This week offered a perfect example of that problem in South Carolina.
---
|
---
**SOUTH CAROLINA** The South Carolina State House just passed its annual budget, and spending **grew by 8 percent over last year.** The **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** fought back.SCFC members introduced over 100 amendments aimed at stripping out some of the most wasteful spending items in the budget. Among the targets were taxpayer funding for climate change research, Hollywood film subsidies, and corporate welfare programs.Each amendment forced lawmakers to go on the record. When the final vote came, the budget passed **101–18**. Every member of the South Carolina Freedom Caucus voted **no** , joined by just two other Republicans.That vote tells the story.When **all Democrats and most Republicans** vote for the same budget in a deep red state, taxpayers can be sure they are the ones getting fleeced. One Democrat in particular, **Rep. Gilda Cobb-Hunter** , even took to social media to brag about the budget's passage. Cobb-Hunter just recently called Moms for Liberty a “terrorist organization.”Despite that record, the **Republican Speaker appointed her to one of the most powerful committees in the legislature, the committee responsible for crafting the state budget.** After the vote, Cobb-Hunter proudly declared that she and the Democrats had stopped the “radical right wing,” meaning the South Carolina Freedom Caucus, from “defunding the government.”Her comment revealed the reality in Columbia.Establishment Republicans and Democrats often operate as a **Uniparty** , working together to protect bigger government and higher spending.The **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** is exposing that arrangement.By forcing vote after vote on wasteful programs, SCFC members ensured that lawmakers supporting this bloated budget will now have to defend those decisions to the taxpayers back home.

clean_body: | | | | Dear Friend, Across the country this week, state Freedom Caucus members were fighting bloated budgets, exposing big-government Republicans, pushing tax relief, and defending constitutional rights.In many state capitols, the biggest fight is not between Republicans and Democrats. It is between conservatives and the Uniparty RINOs who protect bigger government. This week offered a perfect example of that problem in South Carolina. | SOUTH CAROLINA The South Carolina State House just passed its annual budget, and spending grew by 8 percent over last year. The South Carolina Freedom Caucus fought back.SCFC members introduced over 100 amendments aimed at stripping out some of the most wasteful spending items in the budget. Among the targets were taxpayer funding for climate change research, Hollywood film subsidies, and corporate welfare programs.Each amendment forced lawmakers to go on the record. When the final vote came, the budget passed 101–18. Every member of the South Carolina Freedom Caucus voted no , joined by just two other Republicans.That vote tells the story.When all Democrats and most Republicans vote for the same budget in a deep red state, taxpayers can be sure they are the ones getting fleeced. One Democrat in particular, Rep. Gilda Cobb-Hunter , even took to social media to brag about the budget's passage. Cobb-Hunter just recently called Moms for Liberty a “terrorist organization.”Despite that record, the Republican Speaker appointed her to one of the most powerful committees in the legislature, the committee responsible for crafting the state budget. After the vote, Cobb-Hunter proudly declared that she and the Democrats had stopped the “radical right wing,” meaning the South Carolina Freedom Caucus, from “defunding the government.”Her comment revealed the reality in Columbia.Establishment Republicans and Democrats often operate as a Uniparty , working together to protect bigger government and higher spending.The South Carolina Freedom Caucus is exposing that arrangement.By forcing vote after vote on wasteful programs, SCFC members ensured that lawmakers supporting this bloated budget will now have to defend those decisions to the taxpayers back home. | SFCN IN THE MEDIA This week I joined Daniel Horowitz on The Blaze’s Conservative Review podcast for an in-depth conversation about the growing Freedom Caucus movement across the country. We discussed the fights happening in state capitols nationwide, how Freedom Caucus members are challenging the Swamp at the state level, and why the Freedom Caucus model is spreading to more states each year.We also talked about national politics, the recent Texas primaries, and how conservative voters are demanding real leadership from the lawmakers they send to office.You can watch the full interview here: | FREEDOM CAUCUS UNFILTERED - CLIP OF THE WEEK Each week we highlight a clip from our radio show and podcast Freedom Caucus Unfiltered , where we bring you the Freedom Caucus perspective on national and state politics.This week, House Freedom Caucus member Rep. Eric Burlison pulled back the curtain on what Monday nights in Washington often look like.Most lawmakers head to steak dinners with lobbyists.Freedom Caucus members gather together with Chick-fil-A and pizza to discuss how to reduce the size and scope of government.Make sure you subscribe so you never miss an episode. Subscribe on (or on your preferred podcast platform)Follow us on X \- us on TikTok \- us on Facebook \- | QUICK HITS ⚡️Missouri: Eliminating the state income tax has been a top priority for the Missouri Freedom Caucus. This week the Missouri House legislation to eliminate it 98–54. If signed into law, Missouri would join the growing number of states without an income tax. The bill now heads to the State Senate. ⚡️Arizona: Arizona Freedom Caucus Chairman Jake Hoffman had his Second Amendment rights this week after action by President Trump’s Department of Justice. Hoffman had previously been pardoned by President Trump, but lingering federal restrictions still affected his ability to own firearms. All because he dared to question the validity of the 2020 elections. ⚡️Minnesota: The Minnesota Freedom Caucus legislation critics have dubbed the “Rent for Riots” bill , which could provide taxpayer-funded rent assistance to individuals who fought ICE agents and face eviction. ⚡️Illinois: Members of the Illinois Freedom Caucus rolled out a “Solutions Package” ten bills aimed at bringing relief to taxpayers. The proposals include repealing the estate tax, lowering the income tax, restoring school choice, and requiring voter ID for elections. ⚡️West Virginia: The West Virginia Freedom Caucus Republican leadership to return the state’s budget surplus directly to taxpayers rather than using it to grow government spending. The WVFC proposal would return roughly $400 to each taxpayer.⚡️Maryland: The Maryland Freedom Caucus Republican Delegate Jefferson Ghrist for siding with Democrats on a new taxpayer-funded subsidy program. As the caucus put it, Democrats “find many bedfellows in our party here in Maryland.”⚡️Minnesota: MNFC member Rep. Ben Davis a powerful speech opposing a Democrat bill that would ban firearms inside the state capitol. “It appears that you’re all for constitutional rights except for in the people’s house,” Davis said. | HELP US KEEP BUILDING The victories you read about in this email do not happen by accident.They happen because disciplined Freedom Caucus members organize inside state legislatures, stand on conservative principles, and refuse to back down when the political class pushes back. Your support helps expand this model into more states, support our legislators, and expose what is really happening inside state capitols across the country. We'll be back with another update soon. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresident State Freedom Caucus Network | |

Friend, I’m reaching out today because there’s an important election happening in Wisconsin on April 7.
Judge Chris Taylor is running for the Wisconsin Supreme Court — and the stakes couldn’t be higher.
[**In a moment, I’m going to ask you to chip in to support Judge Chris Taylor’s campaign.**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260313_1_ak.tGOwFH&amount=10&refcode=em20260313-1227&t=4&akid=1234%2E294397%2EtkRtyB) But first, let me explain why this race matters so much.
Wisconsin’s Supreme Court will shape decisions that impact reproductive healthcare access, fair elections, and whether working people are treated fairly under the law.
The cases the court oversees aren’t abstract debates. They impact real issues affecting Wisconsinites across the state.
Judge Chris Taylor has spent her career fighting for fairness and equal justice under the law — first as an attorney, then as a public servant, and now as a judge.
She understands that courts should protect people’s rights, not strip them away.
But Judge Chris Taylor won’t win this race on values alone.
Right-wing special interests treat state Supreme Court races like battlegrounds. They pour millions of dollars into states to capture control of the courts, and Wisconsin is next on their list.

body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/gn57LARMqke5xc5N293Q6w2?contactdata=puoxhNZAWLgxjIsLrux44hFcRY4saoxmeECB37bn+2jMyZgEkhMQ6pEkFg09ytC1951C5YqceFaefc907T298T6d46ZgmIox5gY9tGM8k3WLtJRuF4UgFothVq6GN+F4 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/gn57LARMqke5xc5N293Q6w2?contactdata=puoxhNZAWLgxjIsLrux44hFcRY4saoxmeECB37bn+2jMyZgEkhMQ6pEkFg09ytC1951C5YqceFaefc907T298T6d46ZgmIox5gY9tGM8k3WLtJRuF4UgFothVq6GN+F4]
Peter,
The 2026 short legislative session provided Oregon lawmakers with the opportunity to hold global polluters responsible for the financial burdens they have placed on Oregonians as climate catastrophes worsen. Despite the resounding support expressed by Oregonians across the state, lawmakers failed to pass the Climate Resilience Superfund Bill (SB 1541) for basic fairness. Tell your lawmakers how that makes you feel here. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/gn57LARMqke5xc5N293Q6w2]
The Climate Resilience Superfund Bill would have raised billions of dollars in revenue for wildfire prevention and recovery, energy efficient investment, flood protection, resilience for electric power grids, water supply, and farms and fisheries – all without raising taxes on Oregonians.
It is thanks to the support shown by all of you that this bill made it farther in the legislature than ever before during the 2026 session.
Session may be over now, but that doesn’t mean our work to hold polluters accountable has ended, and we aren’t sparing legislators who didn’t stand alongside the thousands of Oregonians for this bill.
Peter, your legislators need to hear from you. Will you take a moment to thank those who supported this bill, and express disappointment for those who did not? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/gn57LARMqke5xc5N293Q6w2]
Take action [https://secure.ngpvan.com/gn57LARMqke5xc5N293Q6w2?contactdata=puoxhNZAWLgxjIsLrux44hFcRY4saoxmeECB37bn+2jMyZgEkhMQ6pEkFg09ytC1951C5YqceFaefc907T298T6d46ZgmIox5gY9tGM8k3WLtJRuF4UgFothVq6GN+F4]
Us everyday Oregonians should not be fronting the cost of the damages from the mega corporations polluting our state. We deserve better. It’s time to make sure our lawmakers continue to hear us.
Together,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Eliza.png]
Eliza Walton (she/they)

clean_body: The moment I knew I had to fight. | | | | | | My heart skipped a beat that day, Peter. When the shot rang out and our President wasn't just still standing, but he held his fist high, blood streaming down his face, and shouted in defiance, "FIGHT, FIGHT, FIGHT," I knew he was right. I had to fight. That was the day I knew I needed to get off of the sidelines and get in the game. That was the day I started to seriously consider running for office. Congressman Jim Jordan and President Trump asked me to run for Congress in 2022, but with my kids still in high school, I just couldn't bring myself to do it. But, watching the scene unfold in Butler, Pa., I knew I couldn't sit it out anymore. Now, I'm fighting. Congressman Jordan and President Trump have already joined my team because they know I'm a proven winner. | | I feel called to run for Congress. God Bless, Jay Feely Republican Candidate for Arizona's 1st District | |

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Another “day in America”
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Friends,
Yesterday, two more communities joined Tucson, Sandy Hook, Parkland, Las Vegas, and far too many others impacted by gun violence: Old Dominion University in Virginia, and the synagogue and day school of Temple Israel in Michigan.
A news outlet called it another “day in America,” but I refuse to accept that. Together, we’ve seen this is not the way things have to be. We can take action to reduce gun violence, we know it works, and we know creating a different world for our children is possible.
This work will always be challenging, but the world we fight for is worth the challenge.
It will take courage to get there. It is through courage that we have already made significant progress. And it is with courage that we continue to face down the reality of gun violence and work to stop it, once and for all.
If you are still with me, please:

**_Crains Detroit:_ Kentucky governor brings red-state playbook to battleground Michigan**
* * *

Peter,

Across the country, Democrats in tough races are looking for a path forward — one that moves past the same old political games and focuses on what actually matters to the people we serve.

_Gov. Andy Beshear knows a thing or two about that._

In Kentucky, he won a statewide race in a state that Donald Trump carried by huge margins. And he did it with a simple approach: **treat people like people, not numbers on a spreadsheet.**

That means talking to voters like adults; using clear language and saying what you mean. Listening to people's concerns and focusing on the issues that actually affect their lives — things like good jobs, strong schools, affordable health care, and safer communities.

It also means refusing to get dragged into the kind of divisive political talking points that dominate cable news but don't solve anyone's problems. It's a common sense approach to leadership. That's the playbook Andy is sharing with Democrats across the country. And most recently, that meant heading to Michigan.

Michigan alone has key congressional races, an open Senate seat, and a gubernatorial race that will help determine the direction of the state for years to come. If we want to keep making progress for working families, we need to keep these seats blue, and elect for-the-people candidates. Andy is doing his part by traveling the country, talking to people on the ground, supporting strong candidates, and sharing the approach that has helped him win tough races, three times.

I am excited to reveal that my 5th book is now available for pre-order: Trump 2.0
This is the first book to examine the consequential impact of Trump's non-sequential terms in office. His ability to come back to office after 4 year of planning and plotting -- the difference that the people, process and policies of Trump 2.0 will make and why they will be historic.
I am honored that President Trump offered to write the foreword for the book -- I am excited to share it with you.
It is available for pre-sale now -- just click the link below. Pre-sales are critical to a book's success so your support is super helpful. Thank you!
**For the first time, I want to share EXCLUSIVELY** with you part of what President Trump wrote:
_" In everything we do, we are fighting for the law-abiding, hardworking_
_people of our country. This is the essence of "Trump 2.0,"_
_and there are few people who understand it better than my friend and_
_former White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer. Sean has been with_
_us since the beginning. He played a central role in helping us defeat_
_Crooked Hillary Clinton in 2016 --and he has been a warrior for our_
_cause ever since._
_If you want to understand the people, the policies, and the process_
_of my second term in office, read this book. I hope you enjoy it, and_
_always remember --the best is yet to come."_

body:
We asked, you answered. Here’s how we move forward. | | | Peter, Immigrant women have long been at the forefront of bringing our communities together. From journalist Jovita Idar, who organized for women’s suffrage and education for Mexican-American youth in the early 1900s, to Elvira Arellano, whose commitment to remain with her U.S.-born son led to the nationwide spread of church sanctuary policies in the early 2000s, women have consistently been at the forefront of reforms that have benefitted everyone. United We Dream continues to uplift women as they organize and lead their communities forward. We’re ensuring women have access to training on how to bring their communities together and discover strategies for building non-violent resistance. Together, we’re building a future where everyone is free to live, speak, and be themselves, and where our communities have access to what they need to thrive regardless of their background. This work isn’t confined to one month — we press on 365 days a year, every year, to keep in the fight. [**Will you help us train women leaders by making a gift today? United We Dream continues to uplift women as they organize and lead their communities forward. We’re ensuring women have access to training on how to bring their communities together and discover strategies for building non-violent resistance. Together, we’re building a future where everyone is free to live, speak, and be themselves, and where our communities have access to what they need to thrive regardless of their background. This work isn’t confined to one month — we press on 365 days a year, every year, to keep in the fight. Friend, A majority of members of Congress are millionaires, not regular people. But now we have a chance to send a community organizer and true public servant to the U.S. Senate to fight for us. As a Florida State Representative, Angie Nixon:
* introduced a resolution for a ceasefire in occupied Palestine
* expanded childcare for thousands of families
* stopped a major grocery chain from price-gouging
* led the fight against DeSantis’s unfair voting maps

But now we have a chance to send a community organizer and true public servant to the U.S. Senate to fight for us. As a Florida State Representative, Angie Nixon: introduced a resolution for a ceasefire in occupied Palestine expanded childcare for thousands of families stopped a major grocery chain from price-gouging led the fight against DeSantis’s unfair voting maps secured funding for quality healthcare and public schools introduced visionary legislation to help people thrive―such as universal child care, tenants’ rights and affordable housing, gun violence prevention, high teachers’ salaries, and life-saving heat protection for workers and people in the prison system As a union organizer and leader of a statewide coalition, Angie has fought for a fair and inclusive democracy and an economy that puts teachers, nurses, and working people over billionaire bullies and greedy corporations. Together, let’s send Angie Nixon to the U.S. Senate to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and ensure the government actually works for the people. | Despite attacks for speaking up for Palestinians’ human rights and liberation, Angie has never backed down from saving lives. She has built a reputation in Florida’s capital as an outspoken fighter who’s not afraid to confront corruption and powerful interests. Angie is also a mother of five and a small business owner, running a bookstore and community hub that provides healthy food and educational opportunities to local families. Friend,
Outside a high school in Breese, Illinois, an area that national Democrats have long abandoned, the Proud Boys put up a massive billboard recruiting young people into their racist, extremist gang:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrrsms-bb?refcode=250930_rrr_billboard [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrrsms-bb?refcode=250930_rrr_billboard]

Our team came together, pooled resources, and put up a billboard of our own — one that called out the Proud Boys for exactly what they are: violent, hate-filled extremists:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrrsms-bb?refcode=250930_rrr_billboard [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrrsms-bb?refcode=250930_rrr_billboard]
And guess what? The Proud Boys’ billboard is now GONE! Taken down. Removed.
But you and I both know this fight doesn’t end in Breese. Extremist groups are recruiting across the country. If we don’t push back, they grow bolder.
Resist Reclaim Rebuild is ready to keep going — to meet hate head-on wherever it shows its face. But we can only do that if our movement has the resources to keep fighting. We can’t let hate win. Together, we won’t.

# Trump demands Powell cuts rates as Iran War surges oil prices
President Trump on March 12, 2026, **[urged Fed Chair Jerome Powell to cut interest rates immediately](https://substack.com/redirect/ad02d8e9-2327-4138-9d42-e6cb6444d06e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid escalating U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran that has pushed oil above $100/barrel, raising energy costs and inflation pressures complicating Fed policy. Trump criticized Powell ahead of the March 17 FOMC meeting.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad02d8e9-2327-4138-9d42-e6cb6444d06e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump Targets Powell Directly** : President Trump posted on Truth Social calling for immediate rate drops, nicknaming Powell "Too Late" and linking delays to economic harm from rising energy prices due to Iran conflict risks in Strait of Hormuz.
* **Oil Prices Spike Sharply** : Geopolitical tensions drove oil past $100/barrel first time since 2022, with gasoline and diesel surging rapidly, pinching consumers and adding to inflation the Fed monitors closely.
* **Fed Faces Political Pressure** : Trump, who nominated Powell in 2017, has long pushed for rates as low as 1%; Powell insists decisions are data-driven, not political, amid ongoing White House tensions.
* **Additional Probe Adds Strain** : Federal prosecutors, under Trump's direction, investigate Powell over Fed headquarters renovation testimony, which Powell called unprecedented pressure on the central bank.

# High oil prices cause market drama but drilling stays flat
Oil prices surged to around $94-95/barrel for WTI and Brent amid Iran-related supply disruption fears, sending global markets into sell-offs, yet energy companies **[resist boosting drilling](https://substack.com/redirect/7eb462cd-0eea-4117-b90a-01f752435ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7eb462cd-0eea-4117-b90a-01f752435ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)due to long-term conservative outlooks and balance sheet discipline.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7eb462cd-0eea-4117-b90a-01f752435ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Geopolitical Risk Drives Rally** : Current high prices stem from risk premium over Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz threats, not fundamental supply-demand shift, with futures still 30-40% above pre-war levels.
* **Companies Prioritize Discipline** : Major firms like Exxon, Chevron focus on conservative decade-long price assumptions rather than short-term volatility, preferring hedging over accelerated activity.
* **Long Timelines Deter Response** : New production investments take years; forward curves predict Brent below $70 and WTI below $65 by 2030 due to expected post-war oversupply of 1-3 million barrels/day.
* **No Boom Expected Soon** : Analysts doubt elevated prices trigger near-term drilling increase, as companies weigh billion-dollar commitments against moderate long-term forecasts.

# Palantir AI gives the West an edge in Middle East War
Palantir CEO Alex Karp stated on March 12, 2026, that the company's AI platforms provide the U.S. and allies **[a critical lethal and coordination advantage](https://substack.com/redirect/fe45c67f-ad12-4a09-a879-8ab48dd72703?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the Middle East conflict against Iran, including real-time data linking and surveillance via Project Maven.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe45c67f-ad12-4a09-a879-8ab48dd72703?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **AI Enhances Lethal Capabilities** : Karp emphasized America's unique AI-driven lethal edge in warfare, with Palantir's software enabling data coordination among U.S. and Middle East partners hit by Iranian attacks.
* **Project Maven in Action** : The AI surveillance tool, using satellite imagery, serves as backbone for operations, potentially including recent U.S.-Israel efforts, with rapid expansion among regional allies.
* **War Targets Digital Assets** : Iran bombed Amazon data centers in the Middle East recently, highlighting attacks on tech infrastructure as national security threats in modern conflict.
* **Karp Defends Role Boldly** : At AIPcon 9, Karp called adversaries "evil" but not stupid, stressing Palantir's unique security product for alliance coordination amid escalating threats.

# US launches forced labor probes on 60 economies
The U.S. Trade Representative opened Section 301 investigations on March 13, 2026, into 60 countries including China, EU, India, and Mexico **[over failures to ban forced-labor goods,](https://substack.com/redirect/e6830de8-0842-4f7a-beec-ebd412327065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e6830de8-0842-4f7a-beec-ebd412327065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)assessing impacts on American workers amid Trump's trade agenda.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e6830de8-0842-4f7a-beec-ebd412327065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Broad Global Scope Targets Enforcement** : Probes examine if foreign governments enforce bans on forced-labor imports, following recent excess capacity investigations into 16 economies.
* **USTR Cites International Consensus** : Jamieson Greer noted widespread failure to block abhorrent practices despite global agreement, threatening U.S. businesses and labor.
* **Timing Raises Summit Concerns** : Launched before potential Trump-Xi meeting and amid Supreme Court tariff limits, experts call timelines unrealistic and risk diluting focus on China.
* **Potential for New Tariffs** : If unfair practices found, tariffs could follow, building on Trump's first-term use of Section 301 against China and EU.

# McDonald's launches $3 Items $4 Meals in value push
McDonald's will **[roll out a"McValue 2.0" menu in April 2026,](https://substack.com/redirect/9f0476d3-f08b-4573-9d00-1cf37bccf3ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** offering $3 items like 4-piece McNuggets and $4 breakfast meals to combat post-pandemic price hike backlash and lure price-sensitive customers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f0476d3-f08b-4573-9d00-1cf37bccf3ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Value Menu Replaces Old Promotions** : McValue 2.0 updates strategy with fixed low prices, addressing affordability complaints from lower-income and millennial diners.
* **Specific Deals Target Basics** : Includes $3 or less for Sausage Biscuit or Chicken McNuggets, $4 combos like McMuffin with hash brown and coffee for budget meals.
* **Response to Price Criticism** : Follows years of hikes drawing social media ire comparing current costs to 1990s lows, with sales gains from prior value efforts.
* **CEO Emphasizes Affordability** : Chris Kempczinski stresses protecting value leadership, with franchisee alignment to meet customer needs amid inflation pressures.

Derek, **If you’re a Pennsylvania Democrat, please keep reading.** Our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline is approaching fast. In the first quarter of a big election year, _everyone_ will be looking to see how much we’ve raised. We’re sure you know that we set fundraising goals every month, quarter, and year — but did you know that in big moments, we break those goals down into smaller chunks? We want to report a strong number this quarter, but we also want to show Republicans that there is real, strong opposition to their agenda in _every_ corner of this country. body:
I might be running for higher office, but I’m still doing the job you already elected me to.
# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4218%2E898137%2E6Qnt6G)
I couldn’t believe it when my constituents told me about a recent story from WDIV. Car insurance companies have been denying drivers’ claims and cancelling their policies because they didn’t list their minor children on their policy — even infants who are _more than a decade_ away from driving or even being able to reach the steering wheel.
I heard that story, and so did many of my constituents. So we decided to fix it. Last month, I introduced Senate Bill 782 to stop this practice.
Traditionally, you were required to list all _eligible drivers_ on your insurance policy application. Then, with the passage of the 2019 Auto No-Fault reform, the language in statute gave insurers the _ability_ to require applicants list all family members, even those not eligible to drive. Some insurance companies claimed this was a new requirement in the law. The state regulator disagreed, leading to confusion and worse — drivers being kicked off their plans _retroactively_ and losing their coverage when they needed it most.
My bill fixes this confusion and provides clarity: requiring insurance companies to return to only requiring eligible drivers to be listed on applications and prohibiting them from canceling plans simply because a non-driving family member wasn’t listed.
That means your insurance can’t bail on you after an accident just because, let’s say, you didn’t list your six-month-old on your policy. **Seems like common sense.**
That’s the kind of work I’ll continue to do in the legislature — even as I’m on the trail — to stop greedy companies from trying to rip people off.
**That’s my pledge to you: I will never stop working to help Michiganders, whether in Lansing or D.C.** [**Can you contribute today to help me fulfill this promise?**](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/1798?t=2&akid=4218%2E898137%2E6Qnt6G)

Jamie Raskin, Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren -- with more and more powerful voices throwing their weight behind abolishing the Electoral College, we are on the verge of a breakthrough!
We deserve a popular vote system in this country to protect our democracy and our rights, from voting to choice and more. RUSH $35 or whatever you can to help ditch the Electoral College forever >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=031326_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
MSNBC: Jamie Raskin thinks the Electoral College threatens democracy. He's right. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=031326_2&amount=25]
There's no greater defender of our democracy than Congressman Jamie Raskin -- and he knows the score, friend. Here's what he had to say:
“ I think that the Electoral College now, which has given us five popular vote losers as president in our history, twice in this century alone, has become a danger not just to democracy, but to the American people . It was a danger on January 6th, 2021. There are so many curving byways and nooks and crannies in the Electoral College that there are opportunities for a lot of strategic mischief. ”
The Electoral College isn’t just a vestige of the past; it is a ticking time bomb for exploitation in our democratic system. Congressman Raskin knows this, which is why he wanted the Jan. 6th Committee to propose getting rid of it. They didn't all agree, so it didn't make their list of final recommendations to Congress.
We know the vote suppressors will do anything in order to win. We have to remove this danger once and for all -- chip in $5, $20, $35 or more to help us end the Electoral College >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=031326_2&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

We don’t necessarily have to wait for Congress to act, either. Movements like the one in favor of the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC) -- an agreement among a group of U.S. states and the District of Columbia to award all their electoral votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the overall popular vote in the 50 states and the District of Columbia -- might end the Electoral College without a constitutional amendment.
16 states plus DC have already joined the NPVIC, accounting for 206 electoral votes and 76% of the states needed to essentially make the popular vote the law of the land. Maine is also moving a bill through their state legislature to join.
Whether it's the NPVIC or something else, it's clear that the Electoral College needs to go.

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

| Winning elections doesn’t start a few weeks before Election Day. It starts _**right now**_ , with organizers on the ground, volunteers talking to voters, and grassroots programs running year-round. Dear Friends and Neighbors, I am so excited to share that the Senate voted to pass the _Renewing Opportunity in the American Dream (ROAD) to Housing Act_. In a town known for gridlock, the bipartisan passage of the ROAD to Housing Act is proof of our dire housing crisis. Families are being priced out of homeownership, rent is out of control, and the dream of a stable home is slipping away from too many Americans. And when most Americans see homeownership as one of the clearest paths to building wealth, we should be doing everything in our power to make that dream attainable.

My parents married young -- 21 and 22 -- and five years later, they bought a modest home. My father was a car salesman. My mother worked as a receptionist. Now, the average age for homeownership is closer to 40. We need to keep fighting for the generations that come after us to do better than we did, not worse.

The ROAD to Housing Act expands the housing supply, reduces red tape, and makes homeownership more affordable. I passed legislation that will help hardworking Maryland families -- and that is worth celebrating.

As a member of the Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, I specifically worked on the following pieces of the package:
• The Bipartisan Community Investment and Prosperity Act
• The Bipartisan Whole-Home Repairs Act
• The HOME Investment Partnerships Reauthorization and Improvement Act
• The Appraisal Modernization Act

As I've said many times before, I don't want our families to live on the margins, but instead I want them to have the opportunity to live beyond their wildest dreams. This will help our young people and families have stable, safe, and affordable homes.

**Fighting This Administration's Disastrous Decisions **
As you know, our nation continues to face self-inflicted challenges. From the President's war with Iran, which has resulted in the loss of U.S. service members and skyrocketing gas prices, to one unqualified person replacing another unqualified person to lead the Department of Homeland Security - I will continue to fight against these thoughtless actions that have real consequences at every turn.
I continue to pray for the families of the 13 U.S. service members who have been killed in Iran since the initial military strikes on February 28. Those men and women gave their lives in defense of all Americans and deserve our gratitude. Additionally, I pray for the service members who have been severely injured and continue to fight for their lives, the dozens of others who have also been injured in this war thus far, and all our service members' families.
Last week, I voted in favor of the War Powers Resolution to end this war. In another act of betrayal against the American people, President Trump has dragged our country into a costly war. In the first two days alone, the United States spent [$5 billion in munitions](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15577.16960198.6004498.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.pbs.org%2fnewshour%2fnation%2fpentagon-says-about-140-u-s-troops-have-been-injured-in-iran-war-so-far-8-severely&redir_log=272149158228811). The Administration's justification for this war is contradictory and constantly shifting. If there were a clear rationale, they would state it. The American people cannot afford this war. Already, brave men and women in uniform have lost their lives for a war with no clear objective and no clear end. Further, Americans will pay for this war at their kitchen tables. That's why I voted for Senator Kaine's War Powers resolution to end this war. The Constitution is clear: the power to declare war belongs to Congress.
And what do Americans have to show for this war? Skyrocketing gas prices at a time when we have a weakened labor market and lower consumer confidence. This war could also eventually affect [grocery prices and even grow inflation](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15577.16960198.6004498.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.washingtonpost.com%2fbusiness%2f2026%2f03%2f12%2firan-economy-oil-gas-inflation%2f&redir_log=691011263989555). Not only did this Administration lie to us when they said they would lower costs on day one, they also lied to us when they said their sole objective was to target the worst of the worst violent criminals for deportation. Instead, much of what we have experienced are Americans killed in cold blood, and the deportation of Dreamers and non-violent migrants who have contributed to our tax base and have only worked to make a life for themselves and their families. DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations across this country have been an unmitigated disaster, and I'm glad Kristi Noem is gone. She needed to go a long time ago, but Senator Markwayne Mullin is as inexperienced and as unqualified as she. I will be [voting NO](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15577.16960198.6004498.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2031712996301369639%3fs%3d20&redir_log=248529407446361) on his confirmation. It's not just the personnel, but it's the ICE policies that need to change, Markwayne Mullin will push the exact same policy as Noem - say "yes" to this President, even as masked men are killing Americans in the streets.
**Fighting Against the SAVE Act**
I know that many Marylanders have contacted my office concerned about the SAVE Act and would like to know my position on it. I will be voting NO.
This legislation seeks to disenfranchise Americans and prevent them from voting. Among those who would be impacted are married women and other Americans who have changed their names; military voters, who would be required to present documentation every time they re-register to vote when their family moves; people of color and low income individuals who are less likely to have documentation like birth certificates and passports; and those who have lived through natural disasters and lost personal documents.

In short, this legislation seeks to disenfranchise voters, not protect election integrity. This is not what the American people want. This is not what Marylanders want. I will vote NO. **Fighting Through Legislation**
It's been a busy two weeks here on Capitol Hill, and I continue to fight for you on the floor of the Senate. From protecting the Chesapeake Bay to providing humanitarian aid to removing President Trump's ability to institute tariffs. These are the pieces of legislation I have introduced or cosponsored:

Professional Degree Access Restoration Act: This bill would reverse recent reductions in federal loan availability for graduate and professional students by amending the Higher Education Act of 1965 to restore the full loan limits that were narrowed under President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act, ensuring students pursuing advanced degrees can access the financial support they need. This bill expands access to advanced education for those seeking to pursue careers in nursing, teaching, social work, medicine, and more.
Maryland Whole Watershed Program Federal Partnership Act: This bill would require the Chesapeake Bay Program Office to participate as an advisory member of the Maryland Whole Watershed Program State Management Team and empower the EPA to contribute to the restoration projects within the Chesapeake Bay Watershed by promoting cross-jurisdictional coordination and providing technical assistance and resources as appropriate. Importantly, the bill ensures that other federal agencies working in the Chesapeake Bay, such as the Army Corps and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), are engaged partners in this innovative pilot program using the Bay Office as a nexus.

These are the bills I have cosponsored:

Supporting Afterschool STEM Educators Act: This bill would establish a dedicated grant program under the Department of Labor to comprehensively support the recruitment and retention of afterschool STEM educators, broadening access and increasing availability for students.
Fair Housing for Survivors Act: This bill builds on protections in the Violence Against Women Act and Fair Housing Act to ensure survivors cannot be evicted or denied access to housing solely for having experienced domestic and sexual violence.
DISCLOSE Act: This bill amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide for additional disclosure requirements for corporations, labor organizations, Super PACs and other entities.
HIV Medication Access Act: This bill amends the Foreign Assistance Act (FAA) to clarify that HIV prevention, including PrEP, is lifesaving humanitarian assistance and that it should prioritize all at-risk populations.
Failed Bank Executives Clawback Act: This bipartisan bill would give the FDIC authority to recoup compensation -- including salaries, bonuses, and proceeds from stock sales -- from senior executives at large banks (those with more than $10 billion in assets) that fail or are placed into FDIC receivership. Introduced after the 2023 failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, the proposal seeks to prevent executives from benefiting from risky management decisions by allowing the recovery of compensation earned in the five years leading up to a bank's collapse.
Direct File Act: This bill would reverse the Trump Administration's decision to end the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Direct File program and permanently authorize the program. This bill would expand access to at least 50% of taxpayers in participating states by tax year 2028, streamline filing by using existing IRS data at taxpayers' option, improve coordination with state tax systems, require annual reporting on usage and access, and reduce fraud by enabling earlier verification of third-party income information.
Housing Tariff Exclusion Act: This bill would create a fast process for exempting homebuilding materials from certain tariffs. It requires the U.S. Department of Commerce to quickly approve tariff exclusions for common construction products and to review other materials if tariffs raise their costs. The bill also applies the exclusions to most tariffs imposed since January 19, 2025, and allows businesses to be reimbursed for tariffs they already paid if an exclusion is later granted.
Access to Fair Financing for Opportunity and Resilient Development (AFFORD) Act: This bipartisan bill would provide added transparency over CDFI Fund operations and strengthen its role in improving capital access and economic development in rural, tribal, and other underserved communities across the country. Additionally, the bill would extend and enhance the CDFI Bond Guarantee Program to enable participation by smaller CDFIs, reauthorizes the CDFI liquidity enhancement program to increase CDFI lending capacity and reach more communities, and bolsters the role of Native CDFIs by expanding a USDA CDFI relending program that partners with Native CDFIs to deploy mortgage loans to eligible Native borrowers.
Supplemental Security Income Restoration Act: This bill would modernize the Supplemental Security Income program by updating outdated income and asset limits that have not kept pace with inflation since the 1970s. It would raise benefit levels, eliminate penalties that reduce benefits for marriage or certain types of support, and simplify the application and payment process. The bill would also extend SSI benefits to residents of Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, and American Samoa.

This change aims to ensure retirement benefits keep pace with inflation and establish parity between the two systems.
WORK to Save Lives: This bill would direct the Department of Labor (DOL), through the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), to issue guidance for employers on obtaining opioid overdose reversal medication and training employees annually on its use. It also requires federal agencies to maintain overdose reversal medication and conduct annual employee training.
Reclaim Trade Powers Act: This bill would repeal Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974. This is the authority President Trump is using for his new 10 to 15 percent tariffs on most imports from most countries.
First Rhode Island Regiment Congressional Gold Medal Act: This bill would award a Congressional Gold Medal to the First Rhode Island Regiment, collectively, which was a Revolutionary War Unit considered the first Black military regiment in U.S. history.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: Trump is betraying the people who voted for him
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Those guys are looking for somebody who is as mad as they are about this, and we can and should be the people they come to.
#

We saw the GOP gut the federal government last year. They told us they had to do it — we’d bankrupt ourselves if we kept helping people. The cost of housing is out of control, but they cut housing assistance. The cost of food is out of control, but they cut food stamps. Nobody can afford their health care, and they pulled a trillion dollars out of Medicaid.
But you know what’s worth a billion dollars a day, our global reputation, and the lives of our kids? A war. We can’t afford to send young kids to college, but we can absolutely send them off to die in some illegal war.
Trump didn’t have much of a presidential platform, but there’s one thing he has always been relentlessly consistent about: No new wars.
Young guys, guys who voted for Trump in 2024 because they believed him on that... They're pissed. They know Trump broke his commitment to them, they know they’ll be the ones fighting this war if it spirals out of control, and they’re taking that as the betrayal it is.
Those guys are looking for somebody as mad as they are about this, and we can and should be the people they come to. But for that to happen, Democrats need to actually do something about this beyond just lip service.
So, here’s somewhere to start: No funding for this war. Trump didn’t bother to make the case for it, he didn’t come to Congress for authorization, and he has no plan to get us out of it. Why the hell would we vote to fund it?
Do you think you can get behind that? If you’re with me, please:
[**Add your voice to the thousands of others who have signed on in opposition to this illegal war with Iran. This is the most important thing we can do right now, and I need your help.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260306-IRAN-EM/?refcode=em260313-1-60&akid=4090%2E734936%2E9wXW9K)
[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260306-IRAN-EM/?refcode=em260313-1-60&akid=4090%2E734936%2E9wXW9K)
Semper Fi,
Ruben

**What happened in Hartford may be a warning sign for religious liberty, medical freedom, and citizen participation across the country.**
Something extraordinary happened in Hartford.
Hundreds of Connecticut residents showed up to testify on vaccine legislation. Thousands more submitted written testimony. Parents, physicians, clergy members, and ordinary citizens drove across the state and waited hours to be heard.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe605d3f-7874-4fe9-8771-2d9cbda9cc9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But many never got the chance.
Speakers were rushed. Testimony was limited. Citizens who had waited all day were cut off when time ran out.
For many in the room, the public hearing felt less like a forum for citizens and more like a process moving toward a predetermined outcome.
That moment is exactly why testimony has now been submitted to the **U.S. Religious Liberty Commission ahead of Monday 's hearing**.
Because what is happening in Connecticut is no longer just a local issue.
It is becoming a **national warning sign for religious liberty and medical freedom**.
* * *
# The Bills at the Center of the Controversy
Two proposals have triggered enormous concern across Connecticut:
**SB 450** and **HB 5044**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c2b489c-4042-4e3a-ac64-611e22128273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
At first glance, they are framed as public health legislation. But many Connecticut residents believe the implications go far beyond routine health policy.
**SB 450** has raised particular alarm because critics argue it could weaken the protections provided by Connecticut's Religious Freedom Restoration Act while litigation related to vaccine mandates is still underway.
That timing has led many advocates to ask a serious question:
Why would lawmakers attempt invalidate the Connecticut's Religious Freedom Restoration Act to defeat the religious freedom lawsuit.
For many residents, that question alone deserves scrutiny.
**HB 5044** has generated concern for a different reason. The proposal expands the authority of public-health officials over vaccine policy, purchasing, and implementation.
Supporters describe the bill as modernization.
Critics worry it reflects a broader trend where authority expands while meaningful exemptions and public participation shrink.
The result is a growing sense among many citizens that decisions are being made **before the public ever enters the room**.
* * *
# Connecticut Residents & Some Legislators Refused to Stay Silent
Despite these concerns, something remarkable happened in Hartford.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/180c29f2-a42e-40f9-8f73-e0fd7538a903?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Citizens showed up.
Parents, physicians, clergy members, and ordinary residents filled the hearing. Thousands more submitted written testimony so their voices would become part of the official legislative record.
Organizations like **CTRAMM** helped mobilize residents, distribute information, and encourage public participation so that lawmakers could not claim the public was disengaged.
**Kate Prokop, founder of CTRAMM** , has played a key role in helping organize citizens, share updates, and ensure residents understand how to participate in the legislative process.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5b2e8ae0-4f0d-418d-b606-fce025013eda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Kate Prokop ([CTRAMM](https://substack.com/redirect/4f703144-07b9-4b39-badd-c45bb3b37dd0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) with State Senator and Gubernatorial Candidate [Ryan Fazio](https://substack.com/redirect/312e9d99-05e5-4fae-b8f5-fd2dd3644f99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Source (Ryan Fazio [Facebook](https://substack.com/redirect/85944e78-c554-4f3a-9ca4-fd8dc6245de5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
The message from Connecticut residents was clear:
**The public is paying attention.**
* * *
# Why This Issue Goes Far Beyond Connecticut
What makes this situation particularly important is that the underlying policy framework is **not unique to Connecticut**.
Across the country, federal funding structures, agency guidance, and regulatory pressure are shaping how hospitals, universities, and state governments implement vaccine policy.
* Institutions often respond by tightening exemption standards.
* Doctors lose discretion.
* Patients lose meaningful pathways for exemptions.
* Religious accommodations become harder and harder to obtain.

_On paper, rights still exist._
In practice, they become extremely difficult to exercise.
That pattern is why the issue is now being raised before a **National Religious Liberty Commission** and why I submitted testimony:
| Goldstein Religious Liberty Commission S...327KB ∙ PDF file
---|---
| [Download](https://substack.com/redirect/5560e27a-e403-4adf-a0f3-8efca18d6a2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
Because if constitutional protections are gradually eroded across multiple states through bureaucratic pressure and legislative maneuvering, the problem is no longer local.
It becomes national and we need a national solution when a state fails its citizens.
* * *
# Why Federal Scrutiny May Be Necessary
Federal oversight is not about controlling state governments.
It is about ensuring that **constitutional protections are not quietly weakened through administrative pressure or legal maneuvering, especially under one-party rule**.
1. When state legislatures consider altering religious liberty protections while litigation is ongoing...
2. When public hearings limit citizen participation...
3. When institutions make exemptions nearly impossible to obtain...

The public has a right to ask whether the balance between government authority and constitutional rights is being preserved.
Those questions are now reaching Washington.
* * *
# What Connecticut Residents Can Do in the Meantime
While the public hearing has concluded, the process is far from over.
The **Public Health Committee still must vote** , and that vote will determine whether **SB 450 and HB 5044** move forward.
When the vote date is announced, it will be critical for residents to return to Hartford so lawmakers feel the pressure **in person**.
But engagement cannot wait until then.
### Email the Public Health Committee
Residents can email members of the committee directly through a link on **[CTRAMM.com](https://substack.com/redirect/2fb5a5d6-2b84-43f1-bf93-2f15af645e12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , which automatically populates the committee's email addresses.
Even a short message opposing **SB 450 and HB 5044** helps ensure Connecticut legislators understand the level of public concern.
Under normal circumstances, lawmakers often pay close attention to the **volume of messages** they receive.
* * *
### Submit Written Testimony
We believe that written testimony continues to matter. While thousands of submissions are already on record, Connecticut residents should submit even more so the official record reflects the strength of public opposition.
Submit testimony here:
[https://www.cga.ct.gov/aspx/CGATestimonySub/CGAtestimonysubmission.aspx?comm_code=PH](https://substack.com/redirect/203851d6-b509-461c-9d1f-bab8605eb1fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When submitting testimony:
• Select **March 11** as the hearing date
• Choose **both SB 450 and HB 5044**
Even short statements become part of the official legislative record.
* * *
### Watch for the Committee Vote
Now we are in the period between the hearing and the committee vote; this is often when **public pressure matters most**.
When the vote is finally scheduled, residents are encouraged to **return to Hartford and attend the meeting** so lawmakers see firsthand that public concern has not faded.
* * *
### Stay Alert to the Legislative Process
Another concern many residents and CTRAMM are watching closely is the possibility of **emergency certification (a.k.a the "e-cert")**, a process that moves legislation directly to the floor and circumvents the normal committee process.
_It has already been used and will likely be used again_
If leadership (the CT Democrats) were to use the e-cert approach on legislation of this magnitude, many citizens would reasonably ask why the normal legislative process was bypassed and what smaller issues are they legislating through e-cert that garner less public attention.
* * *
### Share the Hearing Record Through Social Media
**Share hearing videos, testimony, and transcripts** so more people understand what happened in Hartford. Share Your Story if you submitted testimony or spoke.
* * *
# Why This Fight Is Personal to Dr. Goldstein
**Medical freedom is not an abstract policy debate for me.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b310a11-53f2-49c5-a211-3f8ce7018826?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It is the reason I entered the **congressional arena six years ago** and got involved in politics beyond just knocking on doors for candidates and advocating as President of a medical society. Our advocacy days were just not enough.
As a physician, I took an oath to **do no harm**. Over the past several years, I have watched medical judgment, religious conscience, and patient autonomy steadily pushed aside by political and bureaucratic pressure.
* _Doctors have been sidelined._
* _Patients have been silenced._
* _Citizens have been told not to question policy._

That is not medicine. And it is not freedom.
That is why I am **not backing down**.
The fight for **medical freedom, religious liberty, and patient rights** is one of the defining constitutional battles of our time.
And it will not be won by political insiders.
It will be won by **grassroots citizens who refuse to stay silent**.
Washington has plenty of politicians.
What it needs are **physicians who understand patients, ethics, and the real-world consequences of policy**.
Putting a **doctor in the United States House of Representatives** means bringing real medical experience and patient advocacy back into the legislative process.
But grassroots campaigns run on something simple:
**citizens who care enough to stand up and help.**
Learn more at:

If you are a **grassroots activist** , a parent, a physician, or someone who has been speaking out for medical freedom and constitutional rights, now is the time to help this message spread.

Peter,

A recent headline captured it perfectly: “Republicans Face a Tough Fight to Defend the Senate Majority in 2026.”

Here’s the reality I see every day: If we lose the Senate, our opponents will push their agenda forward without effective checks — and that would hurt Montana families, our borders, our energy security, and so much more.

**As a Navy SEAL who served overseas to protect this country, and now as your Senator fighting for Montana in Washington, I’m committed to doing everything I can to prevent that outcome. **

That’s why I’m personally reaching out today with an opportunity to make your support go further.

I may work in Washington, but home is here in our community. Health care premiums are staggeringly high. Groceries cost more every week. clean_body: | Friend, Our MAGA opponent just bragged that he's been “living and working in DC” and "taking advantage of it" – whatever that means... I’m glad he’s enjoying himself. But when I’m in the Capitol, I work from morning to night to get stuff done for mid-Michigan. And I’m not spending my evenings at fancy receptions – I’m heating up frozen meals after a long day. I may work in Washington, but home is here in our community. And if my opponent spent more time actually talking with the people he’s running to represent in MI-08, he’d know what families here are really dealing with. Gas is over $3.50 a gallon. Health care premiums are staggeringly high. Groceries cost more every week. And working families are stretched thin just trying to keep up. Maybe “taking advantage of it” sounds impressive in DC – but he’s not taking advantage of it for our community. When someone’s focused on DC, it usually means they’re more connected to the political games there than the people back home. That’s exactly what we’re starting to see in this race. National Republicans are already throwing their support behind my opponent, and outside money is pouring into MI-08. It’s no surprise, friend. Election experts say our district could be the “tipping point” race that decides who controls the House. Friend,
Try filling up your car with gas and look at the price... Things shouldn't be this way.
Trump's illegal war with Iran has caused instability abroad and here in our own country.
The high cost of gas at the pump has added yet another negative to the list of problems associated with America's overreliance on oil and gas.
Investing in renewable energy resources through a just transition to a Green New Deal would save us from situations like this and stop our country from being tied to the fossil fuel industry and their need for profit and conquest.
Our environment, our job market, and our wallets would be better off as well.
Friend, I'm not afraid to stand up to the oil and gas industry and fight for real legislative change.
What I am afraid of is what will happen to our earth and our nation if we don't pass a Green New Deal as soon as possible. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. body:
Colorado House committee kills bill requiring abortion providers to offer adoption information
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers voted to postpone a bill [requiring abortion providers to offer adoption information](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) 24 hours before the procedure. Debate also continues over House Bill 26-1246, which supporters say would allow large industrial users to [build their own power generation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), and a Public Utilities Commission sunset bill that could [expand state authority over local land-use](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) decisions. Other disputes involve [compounded weight-loss drugs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and criticism over [raising foreign flags at the Capitol](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) during “friendship” events.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A state audit found major accounting errors in the unemployment insurance division, including [billions in financial misstatements](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Meanwhile, all 66 Democratic lawmakers urged Gov. Jared Polis [not to grant clemency to former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while commentary calls for [independent oversight of election audits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Wolf depredation claims have already [topped $706,000 this year](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), high winds triggered [power-line safety measures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Boulder County, Democrats raised concerns about alleged [“secret” ICE facilities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) based on public data, and Colorado GOP Chair Brita Horn announced [she will step down after the state party assembly](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** A Justice Department review found [tens of thousands of noncitizens listed on state voter rolls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and hundreds of thousands of deceased or departed individuals still registered as officials seek voter data from all states ahead of the 2026 midterms. Debate continues over the [SAVE America Act’s proposed proof-of-citizenship and voter ID requirements](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while reporting highlights claims that multiple FBI counterintelligence investigations [targeted Donald Trump and his allies](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for years. Meanwhile, Palantir CEO Alex Karp said [artificial intelligence could shift economic influence](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) toward vocationally trained, working-class voters, and conservative commentary is [urging more primary challenges](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) against Republican lawmakers who oppose measures like the SAVE America Act.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, March 13, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado House committee kills bill requiring abortion providers to offer adoption information](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
A bill that would have required health care providers to inform women about adoption before performing abortions will not move forward this year after a sharply divided hearing at the Colorado Capitol.
Lawmakers on the Colorado House of Representatives Health and Human Services Committee voted March 10 to postpone indefinitely [Colorado House Bill 26-1105](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) following testimony from witnesses who framed the proposal in dramatically different ways — from a measure supporters said would expand options to one critics argued would insert the state into private medical decisions.
The bill, sponsored by Rep. Ava Flanell, Rep. Scott Slaugh and Sen. Lynda Zamora Wilson, would have required health care providers to offer information about adoption at least 24 hours before performing an abortion — unless the patient declined the discussion.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[HB 26-1246: Protecting Coloradans from rising power costs and a broken system](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY REP. KEN DEGRAAF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Bill aims to shield ratepayers from rising energy infrastructure costs:** House Bill 26-1246 would allow large industrial users to build and operate their own power generation systems instead of relying on utility-built infrastructure financed through higher electricity rates.
* **Proposal targets incentives in Colorado’s utility system:** Supporters argue current regulations encourage utilities to expand transmission lines and other projects because they earn regulated returns on the investments, with the costs ultimately passed on to ratepayers.
* **Supporters say private generation could reduce costs and speed investment:** The bill would allow large facilities—such as data centers—to finance their own dedicated power systems that serve only their operations, potentially avoiding new utility projects while protecting households from paying for the added demand.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
